title: csolution: …Component … uses unknown generator …

The cbuild.yml then lacks the generator's from-pack or path entry.
fix: Check that the generator id in the pack or gpdsc matches a `<generator id=...>` of the pack, or that the external generator is registered in a *.generator.yml in <cmsis-toolbox>/etc; then re-run the generator (`csolution run <name>.csolution.yml -g <generator-id> -c <context>`) so that a consistent gpdsc is written.
note: For components of the project itself, ProcessComponents already fails with 'was not found in global register', so the warning can only come from components added later (gpdsc components); no test reproduces it.

title: csolution: initializing RTE Kernel failed
cause: csolution could not create its internal pack-model kernel at start. The kernel is created on demand independent of project files or options, so this is not caused by the project; it indicates an internal failure such as a broken installation or lack of memory.
fix: Not fixable in the project files. Reinstall CMSIS-Toolbox and retry; if it persists, report it to Open-CMSIS-Pack/devtools with the output of `csolution -V`.
note: Defensive check: ProjMgrKernel::Get() always constructs the singleton, so no input reaches this branch.

title: csolution: initializing RTE Model failed
cause: csolution could not obtain the global pack model from its kernel at start. The model is created together with the kernel, independent of project files or options, so this indicates an internal failure rather than a project problem.
fix: Not fixable in the project files. Reinstall CMSIS-Toolbox and retry; if it persists, report it to Open-CMSIS-Pack/devtools with the output of `csolution -V`.
note: Defensive check; no input path found that leaves the global model null.

title: csolution: missing RTE target
cause: csolution reached component or configuration-file processing for a context that has no RTE target; the target is created when packs are loaded for the context. It is an internal guard that normal project input does not reach, and no test exercises it.
fix: Fix the errors reported before this message (pack loading, device or board selection). If it is the only error, report it to the CMSIS-Toolbox maintainers with the solution that produces it.

message: no packs were found for version check
title: csolution: no packs were found for version check
cause: `csolution check pack-updates` loaded no pack for the selected contexts, so there is nothing to compare with the pack index. That happens when the pack root has no installed packs and the solution names no pack with a local `path:`.
fix: Install the packs the solution needs (`cpackget add <Vendor>::<Pack>` or `csolution list packs -m my.csolution.yml` to see the missing ones) and check CMSIS_PACK_ROOT, then run the check again.

title: csolution: too many command line arguments
cause: The command-line parser reported arguments that it could not assign to an option or to the positional arguments.
fix: Remove stray words from the command line and quote values that contain spaces; `csolution <command> -h` lists the valid options.
note: All positional words go into one catch-all list, of which csolution uses the solution file, the command and its first argument and silently ignores the rest, so this check is hard to reach; no test covers it. The cxxopts submodule was not checked out to confirm when unmatched() is non-empty.

title: packchk M105: Error while parsing command arguments
cause: The packchk command line could not be parsed, for example because of an unknown option or an option given without its value.
fix: Run packchk -h, correct the options, and give exactly one *.pdsc file as the positional argument, e.g. packchk MyVendor.MyPack.pdsc -i ARM.CMSIS.pdsc.
note: No raise site for M105 in packchk at 30f5e81: option errors from cxxopts are printed as '<program> error: <text>' with exit code 1 (ParseOptions.cpp:334-337). Cause inferred from the message text.

message: Only one input file to be checked is allowed.
title: packchk M210: Only one input file to be checked is allowed.
cause: You can only check one PDSC file at a time.
fix: Run packchk once per PDSC; pass packs it depends on with -i instead of as extra file arguments.
note: No raise site for M210 in packchk at 30f5e81; fix inferred from the message and README.

title: packchk M214: Invalid argument: …

note: No raise site for M214 in packchk at 30f5e81 (the code M214 is only raised by svdconv); invalid options are reported by cxxopts as '<program> error: <text>'. Cause inferred from the message text.

message: Component has no condition: 'Cclass=%CCLASS%, Cgroup=%CGROUP%, Csub=%CSUB%, Cversion=%CVER%'

fix: If the component only applies to certain devices, compilers or other components, add a condition attribute naming a <condition> that expresses this; otherwise no change is needed.
note: No raise site for M333 at 30f5e81 (only the progress message M085 'Checking if Component has Condition' exists in the table). Fix inferred from the message and README.

note: No raise site for M345 (nor for the progress message M054 'Checking if URL exists') at 30f5e81; packchk does not test URLs there. Fix taken from the README.

message: Examples found, but no board description(s) found
title: packchk M349: Examples found, but no board description(s) found

Correct the entry for the examples ([/package/examples/example/board](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_examples_pg.html#element_example_board)) or define the board ([/package/boards/board](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_boards_pg.html#element_board)).
fix: Define the boards that the examples reference with <boards><board name="..." vendor="..."> in this pack, or pass the BSP that defines them with -i; otherwise correct the example's <board> reference.
note: No raise site for M349 at 30f5e81; fix inferred from the message and README. Missing boards for examples are reported per example as M324.

message: Generator ID in Taxonomy 'Cclass=%CCLASS%, Cgroup=%CGROUP%' is undefined: '%GENID%'

cause: The generator ID used in the taxonomy is not defined. Define or correct the generator ID ([/package/taxonomy element](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/element_taxonomy.html)).
fix: Define the generator in <generators><generator id="..."> of the same PDSC, or correct the generator attribute of the taxonomy <description>.
note: No raise site for M361 at 30f5e81: CheckTaxonomy reports an undefined generator as M347, and it only runs when the <taxonomy> element itself has a generator attribute (ValidateSyntax.cpp:1834-1870). Fix inferred from the message and README.

title: packchk M373: Unsupported Schema Version: '…'

fix: Set schemaVersion on <package> to a version of the pack schema the tools support, e.g. schemaVersion="1.7.15", and validate against the matching PACK.xsd.
note: No raise site for M373 at 30f5e81; packchk only checks that schemaVersion is present (M376). Fix inferred from the message and README.

title: svdconv M122: Name of command file should follow '@'
cause: An '@', which introduces a command file of options, was given on the svdconv command line without a file name after it.

title: svdconv M203: Value already set: <…> = '…'
cause: In this svdconv version it is raised only for the derivedFrom attribute: an element receives a derivedFrom reference while it already has one. An XML element cannot carry the attribute twice, so a well-formed SVD file should not produce it.
fix: Keep a single derivedFrom attribute on the element at the reported line; if the message persists, report it with the SVD file to Open-CMSIS-Pack/devtools.
note: Attributes are stored in a std::map and processed once per element, so the condition looks unreachable from a file.

message: Parse Error: '%VALUE%' invalid for Array generation
title: svdconv M241: Parse Error: '…' invalid for Array generation
cause: Meant for a dim element whose <name>, <displayName> or <description> has [%s] somewhere other than at the end. In svdconv 30f5e81 the expression parser never returns that result, so such a name surfaces as M239 instead.
fix: Put [%s] at the very end of the name (REG[%s]), or use %s for a list.
note: Unreachable at 30f5e81: ARRAYINVALID is commented out in SvdUtils::ParseExpression (SvdUtils.cpp:140).

message: C Expression: Error occurred during generation!
title: svdconv M247: C Expression: Error occurred during generation!
cause: While writing the System Viewer (SFD) file, an operand of a peripheral's <disableCondition> resolved to an SVD element that is neither a register nor a field, and svdconv wrote '<Error in expression Object>' in its place. Such operands are normally rejected earlier with M248; M247 is the fallback when that check did not apply.
fix: Change the operand to a path that ends at a register or field, for example PERIPH->REG or PERIPH->REG->FIELD (escaped as -> in XML).

message: Dimension expansion exceeds the per-input limit of %NUM% generated indices and model copies.
title: svdconv M249: Dimension expansion exceeds the per-input limit of … generated indices and model copies.
cause: The SVD input declares a dimension (a dim array, for example a register or peripheral replicated with dimIncrement and dim) whose expansion produces more generated indices and model copies than svdconv allows for one input file. The %NUM% in the message is the limit value. The source lines were not available, so this is inferred from the message text and the general meaning of dimension expansion, not checked against the code.
fix: Check the dim and dimIndex elements of the SVD input for very large dimension counts or nested dimension arrays and reduce them, or split the dimension array into smaller groups that stay under the limit. Then rerun svdconv on the corrected file.
note: The source lines were not provided, so the trigger condition and the exact limit could not be verified; the cause and fix above are an inference from the message text and should be confirmed against the README and the source before relying on them.
doc_cause: Reduce the total expanded model size.

message: More than one devices found, only one is allowed per SVD File.
title: svdconv M341: More than one devices found, only one is allowed per SVD File.
cause: The parsed input holds more than one <device> element at the top level. svdconv reads one file per run and an XML document has a single root element, so this does not normally occur.
fix: Keep exactly one <device> per .svd file and describe further devices in files of their own.
note: Not reachable with one well-formed input file.

title: svdconv M342: Dim-extended … '…' must not have <headerStructName>
cause: A cluster that is a dim list (name with %s, expanded into separately named clusters) also has a <headerStructName>; svdconv would ignore the header struct name.
fix: Remove <headerStructName> from clusters that are dim lists.
note: The only raise site is inside '#if 0' (SvdCluster.cpp:582), so svdconv at 30f5e81 never prints M342; cause and fix come from that disabled code and apply to older builds.

message: '<…>' contains more than one '<…> file, PLM may fail
title: csolution: '…' contains more than one '… file, PLM may fail
cause: The RTE folder of a component configuration file (for example RTE/Device/<device>/startup_<device>.c) holds more than one backup with the same prefix, such as two `<file>.base@<version>` or two `<file>.update@<version>` files. The first `<…>` is that folder, the second the prefix (`<file>.base` or `<file>.update`); csolution writes the first match into the cbuild.yml, so the PLM status reported for the file may be wrong.
fix: Keep only the backup whose version is the file's current base version (normally the highest) and delete the stale `.base@`/`.update@` copies, or run `csolution update-rte <name>.csolution.yml`, which deletes redundant backups when it updates the RTE files. Such leftovers usually come from copying RTE folders or from merges in version control.
note: Source comment says the condition 'should never be triggered'; update-rte keeps only file.base@<highest version> and the matching update file. No test reproduces it. The message lacks the closing quote after the prefix.

message: 'compiler' setting in cdefault.yml will be deprecated in CMSIS-Toolbox 3.0.0
title: csolution: 'compiler' setting in cdefault.yml will be deprecated in CMSIS-Toolbox 3.0.0
cause: The cdefault.yml used by the solution (enabled with `cdefault:` in the csolution.yml) sets `compiler:` under `default:`. The setting still works but is announced to be dropped in CMSIS-Toolbox 3.0.0.
fix: Move the compiler selection into the csolution.yml, e.g. `solution: compiler: GCC` (or per build-type/target-type `compiler:`), and delete `compiler:` from cdefault.yml. `select-compiler:` in cdefault.yml carries the same deprecation note in the schema, so move it to the csolution.yml as well.

title: csolution: <command> was not found
cause: The first argument after `csolution` is not a known command (list, check, update-rte, convert, run, rpc), e.g. a typo such as `csolution conver ...`, or only a *.csolution.yml was given without a command. The text `<command>` is printed literally, not replaced by what was typed.
fix: Put a valid command before the options, e.g. `csolution convert <name>.csolution.yml`; `csolution --help` lists the commands.

title: csolution: board mounted device … not found
cause: The board selected with `board:` lists exactly one mounted device in its pack, but that device is not found in the loaded packs, typically because the device family pack (DFP) is not listed under packs: or not installed. The `<…>` is the mounted device as Vendor::Name. The check runs before an explicit `device:` is considered, so setting `device:` does not avoid it.
fix: Add the device family pack that defines this device under packs:, e.g. `- pack: Keil::STM32U5xx_DFP`, and install it with `cpackget add <Vendor::Pack>`.

title: csolution: check <args> was not found
cause: `csolution check` was followed by a subcommand other than `pack-updates`, the only one it knows. The text `<args>` is printed literally, not replaced by what was typed.
fix: Use `csolution check pack-updates <name>.csolution.yml`.

title: csolution: check <args> was not specified
cause: `csolution check` was run without a subcommand. `<args>` is printed literally.
fix: Add the subcommand: `csolution check pack-updates <name>.csolution.yml`.

message: conflict: file '<…>' is declared multiple times
title: csolution: conflict: file '…' is declared multiple times
cause: Within one group of a cproject.yml, clayer.yml or *.cgen.yml, the same `file:` path is listed twice for the same context (after for-context:/not-for-context:/for-compiler: filtering).
fix: Delete the duplicate `- file:` entry, or give the entries disjoint `for-context:`/`for-compiler:` filters.
note: AddFile compares the raw path with already-rebased paths (made relative to the cbuild/cprj folder), so with the default cbuild2cmake backend real duplicates are probably not detected; no test covers this message.

message: cproject not parsed, adding context failed
title: csolution: cproject not parsed, adding context failed
cause: Follow-up error: a project listed under projects: of the csolution.yml could not be loaded, because its cproject.yml was not found or failed YAML or schema parsing, so csolution cannot create its contexts. The message is prefixed with the cproject path.
fix: Fix the error reported before it for the same file (wrong `project:` path, YAML syntax or schema error), then run again.

message: customization of intermediate directory 'intdir' is ignored by the cbuild2cmake backend
title: csolution: customization of intermediate directory 'intdir' is ignored by the cbuild2cmake backend
cause: The csolution.yml sets `output-dirs: intdir:`, which only the legacy `--cbuildgen` flow uses; the default cbuild2cmake backend ignores it.
fix: Remove `intdir:` from output-dirs:; to move intermediate files, set `output-dirs: tmpdir: <path>` instead.

title: csolution: debug-adapters.yml file not found
cause: `csolution list debuggers` reads etc/debug-adapters.yml of the CMSIS-Toolbox installation (the etc folder next to the bin folder that contains csolution), and that file is missing, e.g. a csolution binary copied out of its installation or an incomplete installation.
fix: Run csolution from a complete CMSIS-Toolbox installation with bin/ and etc/ side by side, or reinstall CMSIS-Toolbox.

title: csolution: duplicate CMake image type '…'
cause: In the csolution.yml, a projects: entry with `cmake:` lists two `images:` with the same `type:` (elf, hex, bin or lib). Each output type may appear once per CMake project; the message points to the second `type:`.
fix: Keep one image per type, e.g. `images: - image: build/app.elf  type: elf` and `- image: build/app.hex  type: hex`.

title: csolution: executing generator '…' for context '…' failed
cause: `csolution run -g <id>` started the command of a generator defined in a pack (from its `<exe>` element) for the context, and the command ended with a non-zero exit code. The generator's own output is printed only with `--verbose`, as 'generator ... reported:'. The `<…>` are the generator id and the context.
fix: Run the same command again with `--verbose` to see what the generator reported, and fix that problem (for example a missing tool installation or invalid input); then run the generator again.

title: csolution: export file cannot be written
cause: With `--cbuildgen` and `--export <suffix>`/`-e`, csolution also writes `<context><suffix>.cprj` without fixed pack versions, and that file cannot be saved in the cprj output folder, e.g. the folder is not writable or a folder with that file name exists. The message is prefixed with the file path.
fix: Make the output folder writable or remove what blocks the path, or choose another output folder with `--output`/`-o`.

message: failed to load and insert packs
title: csolution: failed to load and insert packs
cause: A pack description file (*.pdsc) that csolution has to load cannot be read or parsed: an installed pack under CMSIS_PACK_ROOT or a local pack referenced with `packs: - pack: ... path:`. 'Error parsing XML file' messages naming the file follow.
fix: Look at the errors that follow to find the failing *.pdsc; reinstall that pack with cpackget (e.g. remove its damaged folder and run `cpackget add Vendor::Name`), or repair the pdsc of the local pack referenced by `path:`.

message: failed to read latest pack information from pack index
title: csolution: failed to read latest pack information from pack index
cause: `csolution check pack-updates` found no pack information at all: the pack index $CMSIS_PACK_ROOT/.Web/index.pidx is missing or unreadable, and no installed or local pack could be read either. Usually CMSIS_PACK_ROOT points to an empty or uninitialized pack root.
fix: Initialize the pack root with `cpackget init https://www.keil.com/pack/index.pidx` or refresh an existing one with `cpackget update-index`, and check that CMSIS_PACK_ROOT points to it.

title: csolution: file doesn't exist: '…'
cause: The YAML schema check was asked to validate a file that does not exist at the given path (`<…>`). On the command line csolution checks its input files before, so this mostly appears when a client such as an IDE extension, using `csolution rpc`, loads a *.csolution.yml path that does not exist.
fix: Check the solution path the command or the client passes to csolution and point it to an existing `<name>.csolution.yml`.
note: All command-line callers check existence before parsing; RPC LoadSolution does not, which is the only plain path to this message found.

title: csolution: generator '…' was not found
cause: The id given with `csolution run -g <id>` matches neither a globally registered generator nor a generator of a component selected in the context. Ids are case-sensitive and come from the pack's `<generator id=...>`.
fix: List valid ids with `csolution list generators <name>.csolution.yml -c <context>` and pass one of them; check that the component that uses the generator is in the context's components:.

title: csolution: generator executable '…' was not found
cause: The pack generator selected with `-g` has no command for this host: its `<exe>` element lists no `<command>` for the host OS (host attribute win, linux or mac), or the command is a web URL. The `<…>` is the generator id.
fix: Run the generator on a host its pack supports, or update the pack; the pack's documentation tells how to start the tool otherwise.

message: generator executable file '<…>' does not exist
title: csolution: generator executable file '…' does not exist
cause: The pack generator's command resolved to a file that does not exist. Relative commands are taken from the pack folder; a command with a `key` attribute takes its folder from that Windows registry value or, on Linux/macOS, the environment variable of that name. The `<…>` is the resolved path.
fix: Check that the pack is installed completely (reinstall it if the file is missing) and that a tool referenced through a key is installed and its registry value/environment variable points to it.

title: csolution: generator identifier was not specified
cause: `csolution run` was called without `-g`/`--generator <id>`.
fix: Add the generator id, e.g. `csolution run <name>.csolution.yml -g <generator-id> -c <context>`; `csolution list generators <name>.csolution.yml` shows the ids.

title: csolution: list <args> was not found
cause: `csolution list` was given a subject it does not know; the word after `list` must be one of packs, boards, devices, npus, components, configs, dependencies, examples, templates, contexts, targets, target-sets, debuggers, generators, layers, toolchains or environment. A solution file whose name does not end in `.csolution.yml` is also taken as that subject.
fix: Correct the subject, e.g. `csolution list devices my.csolution.yml`, and pass the solution as `<name>.csolution.yml` or with `-s`.

title: csolution: list <args> was not specified
cause: `csolution list` was run without saying what to list.
fix: Add the subject after `list`, e.g. `csolution list packs`, `csolution list devices`, `csolution list components my.csolution.yml` or `csolution list contexts my.csolution.yml`; `csolution --help` lists the choices.

title: csolution: malformed access sequence: '…
cause: A path or value in the YAML (for example under `add-path:`, `define:`, `misc:`, `output-dirs:`, `linker:`, a debugger or image file, or a generator path) contains a `$` that opens an access sequence but has no closing `$`. `<…>` is the whole value after variables were expanded.
fix: Close the access sequence, e.g. `$OutDir(project)$` or `$SolutionDir()$`, or remove the stray `$`.
note: No test produces this message; the MLOps test commented as 'malformed access sequence' (ProjMgrUnitTests.cpp:8025) uses `$BadVar$`, which is closed and leads to 'unknown access sequence' instead.

message: mlops.npu.type value does not match DFP device information
title: csolution: mlops.npu.type value does not match DFP device information
cause: `mlops:` - `npu:` - `type:` in the csolution.yml names an NPU type (e.g. Ethos-U85) that the DFP does not declare as an NPU feature for the processors of the MLOps contexts. The comparison is exact text. The value is still used for the Vela options.
fix: Write the NPU type exactly as the DFP declares it, or remove `type:` so that csolution takes it from the DFP. `csolution list npus my.csolution.yml` shows the types per device.
note: The tests check that this warning is absent in the mismatch and no-NPU cases; none provokes it.

title: csolution: multiple cdefault files were found
cause: The csolution.yml has `cdefault:`, and one of the folders csolution searches for the cdefault file (the solution folder first, then the compiler root, i.e. CMSIS_COMPILER_ROOT or the toolbox's `etc` folder) contains both `cdefault.yml` and `cdefault.yaml`. The message's location is that folder.
fix: Keep only one of `cdefault.yml` and `cdefault.yaml` in that folder.

message: no NPU was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no NPU was found with filter '…'
cause: `csolution list npus -f <words>` found NPUs, but no entry matched all filter words; `<…>` is the filter. A word matches either the NPU line (type and MACs) or one of its device lines (vendor, device, processor, core); matching is case-insensitive.
fix: Loosen the filter, e.g. `-f U55` or a device name part, or run without `-f`.

message: no board was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no board was found with filter '…'
cause: `csolution list boards -f <words>` found boards, but none whose line (`Vendor::Board[:Revision] (Vendor::Pack@version)`) contains all the filter words; `<…>` is the filter. Matching is case-insensitive substring matching, and every word must match.
fix: Use fewer or shorter filter words, e.g. `-f STM32` instead of a full board name, or run without `-f` to see the full list. Without a csolution.yml the list covers all installed packs; with one, only the packs the solution loads.

message: no component was found for device '<…>'
title: csolution: no component was found for device '…'
cause: `csolution list components` with a csolution.yml found no software component in the loaded packs that applies to the context's device; `<…>` is the device. Typically the solution's `packs:` list contains only packs whose components do not match that device, or the device pack has no components.
fix: Add the packs that provide components for the device under `packs:` in the csolution.yml (for example the DFP and `- pack: ARM::CMSIS`), install them with cpackget, and run the command again.

message: no component was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no component was found with filter '…'
cause: `csolution list components -f <words>` found components, but none whose component ID contains all the filter words; `<…>` is the filter. Matching is case-insensitive substring matching and every word must match.
fix: Loosen the filter, e.g. `-f CORE` or `-f Device`, or run without `-f` to see all component IDs.

message: no context was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no context was found with filter '…'
cause: `csolution list contexts -f <words>` found no context name (`<project>.<build-type>+<target-type>`) that contains all the filter words; `<…>` is the filter. Matching is case-insensitive substring matching.
fix: Use a part of a project, build-type or target-type name that exists, e.g. `-f Debug`, or run `csolution list contexts my.csolution.yml` without `-f`.

message: no device was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no device was found with filter '…'
cause: `csolution list devices -f <words>` found devices, but none whose line (`Vendor::Device[:Pname] (Vendor::Pack@version)`) contains all the filter words; `<…>` is the filter. Matching is case-insensitive substring matching and every word must match.
fix: Loosen the filter (e.g. `-f STM32U5`), or run without `-f`. If the device belongs to a pack that is not installed, install it with `cpackget add <Vendor>::<Pack>`.

title: csolution: no installed NPU was found
cause: `csolution list npus` found no NPU: none of the devices in the loaded packs (or, with a csolution.yml, the device of the selected contexts) declares an NPU feature (`<feature type="NPU">`) in its DFP.
fix: Install the DFP of a device with an NPU (for example an Ethos-U based device) or select a context whose device has one. Run `csolution list devices` to check which devices are loaded.

title: csolution: no installed board was found
cause: `csolution list boards` found no board in the packs it loaded: the CMSIS pack root has no pack that describes boards, or the csolution.yml given restricts loading to `packs:` that contain no boards.
fix: Install a board support pack, e.g. `cpackget add <Vendor>::<Board>_BSP`, and check that CMSIS_PACK_ROOT points to the pack root in use. With a csolution.yml, add the BSP under `packs:`.

title: csolution: no installed component was found
cause: `csolution list components` without a solution context found no software component in the installed packs, which usually means the CMSIS pack root is empty or holds no pack with components.
fix: Install packs with cpackget (for example `cpackget add ARM::CMSIS`) and check that CMSIS_PACK_ROOT points to that pack root. To list components for a device, pass the csolution.yml.

title: csolution: no installed device was found
cause: `csolution list devices` found no device in the packs it loaded: the CMSIS pack root has no device family pack (DFP), or the csolution.yml given loads only `packs:` without devices.
fix: Install the DFP, e.g. `cpackget add Keil::STM32U5xx_DFP`, and check CMSIS_PACK_ROOT. With a csolution.yml, add the DFP under `packs:`.

message: no pack was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no pack was found with filter '…'
cause: `csolution list packs -f <words>` found packs, but none whose line (`Vendor::Pack@version` and, when shown, its path) contains all the filter words; `<…>` is the filter. Matching is case-insensitive substring matching.
fix: Loosen the filter (e.g. `-f CMSIS`) or run without `-f`. A pack that is not installed does not appear; install it with `cpackget add <Vendor>::<Pack>`.

message: no packs were found for version check with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no packs were found for version check with filter '…'
cause: `csolution check pack-updates` with `-f <words>` found packs, but no result line (`Vendor::Pack@version -> newer` or `(up-to-date)`) contains all the filter words; `<…>` is the filter.
fix: Loosen the filter, e.g. the pack name only, or run the check without `-f`.

message: no unresolved dependency was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no unresolved dependency was found with filter '…'
cause: `csolution list dependencies -f <words>` or `csolution list configs -f <words>` produced entries, but none contains all the filter words; `<…>` is the filter. Both commands print this same text, so for `list configs` it means that no configuration file matched the filter, not anything about dependencies.
fix: Loosen the filter or run the command without `-f` to see all unresolved dependencies or all configuration files of the selected contexts.
note: The cited line 4509 is in ListConfigs; ListDependencies raises the identical text at line 4544.

title: csolution: node '…' shall contain mapping elements
cause: A node that must hold key/value pairs is written as a scalar or empty in a csolution, cproject, clayer, cbuild-pack or cbuild-set YAML file; `<…>` is the node, with file, line and column. The nodes checked are `processor:`, `output-dirs:`, `generators:`, `rte:` and `west:`. A key left without a value (`processor:` with nothing indented under it) also counts.
fix: Write the node as a mapping with indented keys, e.g. `processor:` followed by `  trustzone: secure`, or remove the empty node.

message: number must be integer or hexadecimal prefixed by 0x
title: csolution: number must be integer or hexadecimal prefixed by 0x
cause: A numeric node holds a value that is neither a plain decimal integer nor a hexadecimal number written with a lowercase `0x` prefix; the message carries file, line and column. The nodes checked are `debugger:` - `clock:`, the `memory:` entries' `start:`, `size:`, `ram-start:` and `ram-size:`, and the `images:` entries' `load-offset:`. Values like `1.5`, `-4`, `1e6`, `64K` or `0X1000` are rejected.
fix: Write the value as a decimal integer (`clock: 10000000`) or as `0x`-prefixed hex (`start: 0x20000000`).

title: csolution: parsing installed packs failed
cause: csolution wanted to load the installed packs (no pack is required by the YAML, or `-l all`/`-l latest` is set) but has no pack root: CMSIS_PACK_ROOT is not set and no default location could be derived from the user environment.
fix: Set CMSIS_PACK_ROOT to the pack folder, e.g. `export CMSIS_PACK_ROOT=$HOME/.cache/arm/packs`, and initialise it with `cpackget init` if it does not exist yet.

title: csolution: processing contexts list failed
cause: `csolution list contexts` could not produce a list: a `-f` filter matched no context (the line before reports `no context was found with filter`), or the solution yielded no contexts at all.
fix: Fix the error printed before it; drop or loosen `-f`, and check that the csolution.yml has `projects:` and `target-types:`.

message: project descriptors 'project', 'west', and 'cmake' are mutually exclusive
title: csolution: project descriptors 'project', 'west', and 'cmake' are mutually exclusive
cause: One entry under `projects:` in the csolution.yml has more than one of `project:`, `west:` and `cmake:`; the message points to that entry. Each entry describes exactly one project. The schema check reports the same problem, so this message appears mainly with `-n`.
fix: Split the entry into separate list items, one with `- project: ...`, another with `- west: ...` or `- cmake: ...`.

message: type '<…>': it must start with '.' or '+' for normal strings and with '^' or '\' for regex patterns
title: csolution: type '…': it must start with '.' or '+' for normal strings and with '^' or '\' for regex patterns
cause: A `for-context:` or `not-for-context:` entry does not begin with `.` (build type), `+` (target type), `^` or `\` (regular expression); `<…>` is the entry, e.g. `Debug` or `CM0+Debug`. The schema rejects such values too, so this message appears mainly with `-n`.
fix: Start the entry with the right prefix: `.Debug`, `+CM0`, `.Debug+CM0`, or a regex such as `^\.Debug\+.*`.

title: packchk M103: Internal Error: …
cause: During the letter-case check of a file path from the PDSC, packchk could not find one path segment in the folder listing although the file exists; the text reads 'Internal Error: file/folder "<segment>" not found'. A doubled slash such as "Files//test.c" produces an empty segment and triggers it.
fix: Look at the segment named in the message and fix the path in the PDSC: remove doubled or stray slashes and make every folder and file name match the name on disk.
note: Only raise site is CheckFiles::CheckCaseSense; the README advice 'Contact Arm' does not explain it.

title: packchk M108: Reading PDSC File failed!
cause: XML parsing of the PDSC file failed. Verify syntax of the PDSC file.
fix: Fix the XML syntax errors that the XML reader reports just before M108 with line numbers (for example a missing end tag, or a bare '&' or '<' in text that must be written & or <), then run packchk again; until the PDSC parses, the later checks have no model to work on.

title: packchk M202: No PDSC input file specified
cause: packchk got no PDSC file to check: no file argument was given, or the argument names a folder instead of a *.pdsc file.
fix: Pass the path of the pack's .pdsc file as the positional argument, not the pack folder, e.g. packchk ./MyVendor.MyPack.pdsc.
doc_cause: Correct the command line. **packchk** expects a *.pdsc file name as input.

title: packchk M203: Error reading PDSC file(s) '…'!
cause: The folder that contains the PDSC holds more than one *.pdsc file, so packchk does not read the pack; M206 printed just before lists the files. Despite its text, M203 is not a content error of the PDSC.
fix: Remove or rename the extra .pdsc files (old copies, backups) in the PDSC's folder, or add --ignore-other-pdsc when they must stay.
doc_cause: Verify the PDSC file for consistency.

title: packchk M205: Cannot create Pack Name file '…'
cause: Check the disk space or your permissions. Correct the path name.
fix: Give -n a path where packchk may write (it creates missing folders itself), e.g. -n build/packname.txt, and make sure the path is not an existing folder and the location is writable.

message: Multiple PDSC file found in package: %FILES%
title: packchk M206: Multiple PDSC file found in package: …
cause: The folder that contains the PDSC holds more than one *.pdsc file; only that folder is searched, not its subfolders. A pack may contain only one PDSC.
fix: Delete the other .pdsc files from the pack root or move them out of the pack, or run with --ignore-other-pdsc if they must stay.
doc_cause: Only one PDSC file is allowed in a package. Remove unnecessary PDSC files. The message lists all \*.pdsc files found.

message: PDSC file name mismatch!   Expected: '%PDSC1%.pdsc'   Actual  : '%PDSC2%.pdsc'
title: packchk M207: PDSC file name mismatch! Expected: '….pdsc' Actual : '….pdsc'
cause: The PDSC file name is not <vendor>.<name>.pdsc as built from the <vendor> and <name> elements of the PDSC (exact, case-sensitive comparison). 'Expected' shows the name built from the elements, 'Actual' the file name.
fix: Rename the PDSC to <vendor>.<name>.pdsc, or correct <vendor> or <name>, e.g. file MyVendor.MyPack.pdsc with <vendor>MyVendor</vendor> and <name>MyPack</name>.
doc_cause: The PDSC file expected has not been found. Rename or exchange the PDSC file.

message: Found blank char '%NUM%' in Packname output filename, deleted
title: packchk M213: Found blank char '…' in Packname output filename, deleted
cause: The file name given with option -n (text file that receives the pack name) contains a space, tab, carriage return or line feed. packchk deletes each such character from the whole path, folder names included, and prints its decimal character code (32 is a space), so the file is written to a different path than the one given.
fix: Give -n a path without blanks, e.g. -n out/packname.txt, so the pack name file lands where the build script expects it.

title: packchk M216: Unable to get executable path …!
cause: packchk was started without --xsd and without --disable-validation, so it looks for PACK.xsd relative to its own executable, but the operating system did not return the executable's path; %MSG% is the system error text. The PDSC is not involved.
fix: Pass the schema explicitly with --xsd <path>/PACK.xsd, or skip schema validation with --disable-validation; otherwise start packchk from a normal, readable installation folder.

message: Either attribute '%TAG%' or '%TAG2%' + '%TAG3%' must be specified for 'memory'
title: packchk M307: Either attribute '…' or '…' + '…' must be specified for 'memory'
cause: `<memory>` element requires that either attribute id or attributes name and access are specified, but none of those were found. Specify the expected attributes. Refer to [/package/devices/family/.../memory](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_memory).
fix: Describe each memory either with id (legacy IROM1/IRAM1 form) or with name plus access, e.g. <memory name="Flash" access="rx" start="0x08000000" size="0x00080000" startup="1"/>.

message: Filename mismatch (case sensitive):   PDSC name : '%PDSC%'   Filename  : '%SYSTEM%'
title: packchk M310: Filename mismatch (case sensitive): PDSC name : '…' Filename : '…'
cause: Filenames are case sensitive. Correct spelling.
fix: Change the path in the PDSC so every folder and file name has exactly the letter case used on disk, or rename the files; 'Filename' in the message shows the on-disk spelling.

title: packchk M311: Redefinition of '…' : '…', see Line …
cause: Two <memory> elements that apply to the same device and processor (including memories inherited from family and subFamily) have the same name, or the same id when name is absent.
fix: Give each memory region a unique name (or id), or remove the duplicate definition.
doc_cause: Remove the redefinition of element _'TAG'_ with name _'NAME'_.

message: Invalid URL / Paths to Drives are not allowed in Package URL: '%URL%'
title: packchk M315: Invalid URL / Paths to Drives are not allowed in Package URL: '…'
cause: The <url> of the package has ':' as its second character, i.e. it starts with a drive letter such as "C:/packs/" instead of a web address.
fix: Set <url> to the web location the pack is downloaded from, e.g. <url>https://www.myvendor.com/pack/</url>.

title: packchk M321: DS5 project requires '.project' file.
cause: An <example> has an <environment name="DS5"> (name compared case-insensitively) whose load path does not end in an Eclipse '.project' file.
fix: Set load to the example's .project file, relative to the example folder, e.g. <environment name="DS5" load=".project"/>, and ship .project and .cproject in that folder.

title: packchk M322: Associated File/Path not found: '…'
cause: An <example> has an <environment name="DS5"> whose load points to a '.project' file, but the matching '.cproject' file next to it is missing from the pack; %PATH% is the full path packchk looked for.
fix: Add the Eclipse .cproject file beside the .project file in the example folder, or correct the load path.

message: Board '%NAME%' redefined, already defined in Line %LINE%: '%PATH%'
title: packchk M325: Board '…' redefined, already defined in Line …: '…'
cause: Two <board> elements in the checked PDSC have the same name and revision. The line numbers are swapped: the message is reported at the earlier board and its 'Line' names the later one.
fix: Remove the duplicate <board>, or give the boards different name or revision values.
doc_cause: This board has been defined already in the line _'LINE'_ of the file _'PATH'_. Verify and remove one of the board definitions. Refer to [/package/boards/board](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_boards_pg.html#element_board).

message: Version not set for Release Information '%DESCR%'
title: packchk M328: Version not set for Release Information '…'
cause: The release defined through the description _'DESCR'_ requires the attribute `<version>`. Refer to [/package/releases/release](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/element_releases.html#element_release).
fix: Add the version attribute to the <release>, e.g. <release version="1.2.0" date="2026-01-31">...</release>.

message: Condition redefined: '%COND%', already defined in Line %LINE%
title: packchk M330: Condition redefined: '…', already defined in Line …
cause: The condition has been defined already in a previous line. Correct the condition name, or remove the duplicate. Refer to [/package/conditions/condition](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_conditions_pg.html#element_condition).
fix: Give one of the conditions a unique id (and update the condition attributes meant to use it), or delete the duplicate.

title: packchk M331: Condition unused: '…'
cause: A <condition> is defined in <conditions>, but no element refers to it through a condition attribute, neither directly nor through another condition.
fix: Delete the unused condition or reference it where intended, e.g. <component ... condition="MyCondition">; suppress with -x M331 if it is kept on purpose.
doc_cause: The condition has been defined but not used further. Remove the condition or add condition rules. Refer to [/package/conditions/condition](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_conditions_pg.html#element_condition).

message: Component 'Cclass=%CCLASS%, Cgroup=%CGROUP%, Cversion=%CVER%' is member of the Cclass='%CCLASS%' which shall contain device specific components.   No condition id set to specify a rule filtering for a device or set of devices.
title: packchk M335: Component 'Cclass=…, Cgroup=…, Cversion=…' is member of the Cclass='…' which shall contain device …
cause: A component with Cclass "Device", "Board Support", or "CMSIS Driver" without Csub has no condition attribute, so nothing restricts it to the devices it supports.
fix: Add a condition that requires the supported devices and reference it from the component, e.g. <condition id="ARMCM4"><require Dvendor="ARM:82" Dname="ARMCM4*"/></condition> and <component Cclass="Device" Cgroup="Startup" ... condition="ARMCM4">.
doc_cause: A component defined as 'board support' needs a reference to a device. Add a device or correct the component definition. Refer to attribute _Cclass_ of [/package/components/.../component](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_component) and [/package/boards/board/mountedDevice](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_boards_pg.html#element_board_mountedDevice).

message: Component 'Cclass=%CCLASS%, Cgroup=%CGROUP%, Cversion=%CVER%, condition=%COND%' is member of the Cclass='%CCLASS%' which shall contain device specific components.   The referenced condition id does not contain a rule filtering for a device or set of devices.
title: packchk M336: Component 'Cclass=…, Cgroup=…, Cversion=…, condition=…' is member of the Cclass='…' which shall …
cause: A component with Cclass "Device", "Board Support", or "CMSIS Driver" without Csub has a condition, but neither that condition nor the conditions it references contains an expression whose Dname matches a device known to packchk (this pack or PDSC files passed with -i).
fix: Add <require Dvendor="..." Dname="..."/> for the supported devices to the component's condition and make sure those devices exist in this pack or in a PDSC passed with -i; M364 lines name Dname values that matched no device.
doc_cause: Define the device [/package/devices/family/../device](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_device) or correct the information about the device in the reference.

title: packchk M338: No releases found!
cause: The PDSC has no <releases> element at all. packchk then also skips the package description and PDSC file name checks.
fix: Add <releases> under <package> with at least one release, newest first: <releases><release version="1.0.0" date="2026-01-31">Initial release</release></releases>.
doc_cause: The PDSC file is missing release information. Add `<release>` information to the file. Refer to [/package/releases element](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/element_releases.html).

message: File with '%COMP%' dependency must have extension '%EXT%': '%PATH%'
title: packchk M341: File with '…' dependency must have extension '…': '…'
cause: An assembler file (category sourceAsm, or category source with extension .s or .asm) has a condition that requires or accepts Tcompiler="GCC", and its extension is lowercase .s; packchk asks for uppercase .S for GCC.
fix: Rename the file to .S and update its name attribute, e.g. name="Source/GCC/startup_device.S".
doc_cause: The file _'PATH'_ with dependency on component _'COMP'_ must have a specific extension _'EXT'_. Verify the dependency and correct the file extension. Refer to [/package/.../files/file](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_file).

message: File with attribute '%ATTR%' must not have category '%CAT%': '%PATH%'
title: packchk M342: File with attribute '…' must not have category '…': '…'
cause: A <file> with attr="template" also has category="include"; packchk does not allow templates to be include folders. Only attr="template" is checked here, not attr="config" as the README example says.
fix: Give the template a file category such as sourceC or header, or remove attr="template" from the include entry.
doc_cause: File _'PATH'_ is defined with the attribute attr set to _'ATTR'_. This conflicts with the file category _'CAT'_ specified in category attribute. For example attr=config and category=include are not allowed for the same file. Correct the file attribute or the file category. Refer to [/package/.../files/file](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_file).

title: packchk M343: File with attribute '…' requires '…' attribute: '…'
cause: File _'PATH'_ is defined with the attribute _'ATTR'_ that requires presense of attribute _'ATTR2'_ as well, but such attribute was not found. For example, attr=template requires that attribute select is defined. Add the required attribute _'ATTR2'_ or correct the attribute _'ATTR'_ in the `<file>` element. Refer to [/package/.../files/file](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_file).
fix: Add select with a short label for the template, e.g. <file category="sourceC" attr="template" name="Templates/main.c" select="Main module"/>.

title: packchk M344: File shall have condition containing '…': '…'
cause: A library or assembler file (category library or sourceAsm, or category source with extension .s or .asm) has no condition with a Tcompiler expression, neither on the <file> nor on its <component>. %COND% is always 'Tcompiler'.
fix: Add a condition that requires the compiler and attach it to the file or its component, e.g. <condition id="GCC"><require Tcompiler="GCC"/></condition> and <file category="sourceAsm" name="Source/GCC/startup.S" condition="GCC"/>.
doc_cause: File definition for _'PATH'_ shall contain a condition _'COND'_. Add attribute condition with the _'COND'_ in the `<file>` tag that defines the _'PATH'_ file. Refer to [/package/.../files/file](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_file).

message: Generator ID in Component 'Cclass=%CCLASS%, Cgroup=%CGROUP%, Cversion=%CVER%' is undefined: '%GENID%'
title: packchk M347: Generator ID in Component 'Cclass=…, Cgroup=…, Cversion=…' is undefined: '…'
cause: The generator ID used in the component could not be found. Verify and correct the generator ID ([/package/components/.../component](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_component)), or define the generator ID (ref [/package/generators/generator](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_generators_pg.html#element_generator)).
fix: Define the generator in the same PDSC, <generators><generator id="MyGenerator">...</generator></generators>, or correct the component's generator attribute to an existing generator id.
note: The component check is skipped when the pack has no <generators> element (CheckComponents.cpp:121-122). The taxonomy check compares the generator attribute of the <taxonomy> element rather than that of each <description> and reports M347, not M361 (ValidateSyntax.cpp:1834-1870).

title: packchk M350: No '…' component found for […] '…' (Compiler: … […])
cause: For a device (checked per processor, per TrustZone mode when Dtz is set, and per compiler named in the pack's conditions), no Device:Startup component (Cclass="Device" Cgroup="Startup") is available whose conditions accept that device. packchk looks in this pack and in PDSC files given with -i.
fix: Add a Device:Startup component with a condition matching the device, or widen its condition (Dname pattern, Dvendor, Tcompiler) to cover the reported device and compiler; if the startup code comes from another pack, pass that PDSC with -i.
doc_cause: The package ([/package](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#element_package)) defines a Vendor-MCU combination for which no component was defined. Define a component ([/package/components/.../component](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_component)) or verify the _'VENDOR'_ - _'MCU'_ settings.

message: Not all Component Dependencies for 'Cclass=%CCLASS%, Cgroup=%CGROUP%, Csub=%CSUB%, Cversion=%CVER%, Capiversion=%APIVER%' can be resolved.%MSG%
title: packchk M362: Not all Component Dependencies for 'Cclass=…, Cgroup=…, Csub=…, Cversion=…, Capiversion=…' can be …
cause: Some of the component dependencies could not be resolved. The message might contain additional information. Verify and correct component definition and dependency information. Refer to [/package/components/.../component](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_component) attribute _condition_.
fix: Read the M502/M504 lines that follow; they name the dependency that fails. Provide the required component or API in this pack, pass the providing pack's PDSC with -i (e.g. ARM.CMSIS.pdsc for CMSIS:CORE), or correct Cclass/Cgroup/Csub/Capiversion in the condition. -x M362 also suppresses M502 and M504.
note: Bug at 30f5e81: bOk in TestComponentDependencies is set before the component loop and never reset (ValidateSemantic.cpp:890, 950), so after the first failing component every later component is also reported with M362.

message: No API defined for Component 'Cclass=%CCLASS%, Cgroup=%CGROUP%, Csub=%CSUB%, Cversion=%CVER%, Capiversion=%APIVER%'
title: packchk M363: No API defined for Component 'Cclass=…, Cgroup=…, Csub=…, Cversion=…, Capiversion=…'
cause: A component has Capiversion, but no <api> with the same Cclass and Cgroup (and a compatible version) is defined in this pack or in a PDSC passed with -i.
fix: Add the API to <apis> (<api Cclass="..." Cgroup="..." Capiversion="...">), pass the pack that defines it with -i, or remove Capiversion if the component implements no API.
doc_cause: The package is missing the API information for the specified component. Refer to [/package/apis](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_apis_pg.html#element_apis).

title: packchk M364: No Devices for Condition '… […] …' available.
cause: The specified condition refers to a device that does not exist. Define the device ([/package/devices/family/../device](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_device)) or correct the information for the condition ([/package/conditions/condition](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_conditions_pg.html#element_condition)).
fix: Correct Dname (and Dvendor) in the condition expression to an existing device or variant, or pass the DFP's PDSC with -i so its devices are known.

title: packchk M365: Redefined … '…' found, see Line …
cause: Two device leaves of the same kind (two <device> elements without variants, or two <variant> elements) have the same name in the PDSC.
fix: Rename or remove one of them so that every Dname and Dvariant is unique.
note: At 30f5e81 the function that raises M365 (ValidateSyntax::CheckDevices) is never called from Check(); the same duplication is reported as M392.
doc_cause: Remove duplicate device/variant entries. Refer to [/package/devices/family/../device](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_device).

title: packchk M366: Redefined … as … '…' found, see Line …
cause: The same name is used once for a <device> without variants and once for a <variant>, so one leaf device is defined as both.
fix: Rename one of them so that every Dname and Dvariant is unique.
note: At 30f5e81 the function that raises M366 (ValidateSyntax::CheckDevices) is never called from Check(); the same duplication is reported as M392.
doc_cause: Device has been redefined as variant or vice versa. Remove duplicate device/variant entries. Refer to [/package/devices/family/../device](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_device).

title: packchk M368: Cannot check '…'…
cause: A <compatibleDevice> element of a <board> has no Dname attribute (for example it only gives Dfamily or DsubFamily), so packchk cannot look the device up; the message reads "Cannot check 'compatibleDevice', no 'Dname' could be calculated".
fix: Give every <compatibleDevice> a Dname and Dvendor, one element per device, e.g. <compatibleDevice deviceIndex="0" Dvendor="ARM:82" Dname="ARMCM3"/>.

message: URL is not conformant: '%URL%':   Backslashes are not allowed in URL, use forward slashes.
title: packchk M370: URL is not conformant: '…': Backslashes are not allowed in URL, use forward slashes.
cause: A path attribute or license entry in the PDSC holds a URL (http, https, ftp or ftps) that contains backslashes.
fix: Write the URL with forward slashes only.
doc_cause: Use standard URL notation using forward slashes (/).

message: %SECTION% Feature for '%MCU%': '%FEATURE%' misspelled, did you mean '%KNOWNFEATURE%' (%DESCR%).
title: packchk M372: … Feature for '…': '…' misspelled, did you mean '…' (…).
cause: This feature _'FEATURE'_ resembles the feature _'KNOWNFEATURE'_. Correct the feature ([/package/devices/family/.../feature](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_feature)) if this is a typo.
fix: Write the type with the spelling suggested in the message, e.g. type="UART" instead of type="Uart".
note: For board features the name in the message is the feature's name attribute, not the board name (ValidateSyntax.cpp:1225).

message: While checking Feature for '%MCU%': Pname '%CPU%' not found.
title: packchk M374: While checking Feature for '…': Pname '…' not found.
cause: A <feature> or <algorithm> of a device has a Pname that matches no <processor Pname> of that device, including processors inherited from family and subFamily.
fix: Correct Pname to one of the device's processor names, or add the missing <processor Pname="..."> definition.
doc_cause: The processor could not be found for the specified device. Refer to [/package/devices/family/../device](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_device) and [/package/devices/family/.../processor](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_processor).

title: packchk M375: No <mountedDevices> for Board '…' found.
cause: If a board element does not contain a `<mountedDevice>` element, then the examples for this board are not shown and example projects may not appear in the development tools. Refer to [/package/boards/board/mountedDevice](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_boards_pg.html#element_board_mountedDevice) of [/package/boards](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_boards_pg.html#element_boards).
fix: Add the device the board carries: <mountedDevice deviceIndex="0" Dvendor="ARM:82" Dname="ARMCM4"/>. The message says <mountedDevices>; the element is <mountedDevice>.

title: packchk M377: File '…' … must have 'attr="config"'
cause: In a Device:Startup component (Cclass="Device" Cgroup="Startup"), a startup_* file or a system_*.c file of category source, sourceAsm or sourceC lacks attr="config". %TYPE% shows the category.
fix: Add attr="config" and a version to these files, e.g. <file category="sourceC" attr="config" name="Source/system_ARMCM4.c" version="1.0.0"/>.
doc_cause: The category _'TYPE'_ of the file _'NAME'_ requires it to be defined as a configuration file. Add the attribute attr="config" to the `<file>` element that defines the file. Refer to [/package/.../files/file](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_file).

message: Component 'Cclass=%CCLASS%, Cgroup=%CGROUP%, Csub=%CSUB%, Cversion=%CVER%, implements the API defined in '%NAME%' but does not attribute 'Capiversion' specifying the version it implements.
title: packchk M378: Component 'Cclass=…, Cgroup=…, Csub=…, Cversion=…, implements the API defined in '…' but does not …
cause: Add attribute Capiversion specifying the API version that is implemented in the component described in the message. Refer to [/package/components/.../component](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_component).
fix: Add Capiversion with the API version the component implements, e.g. <component Cclass="CMSIS Driver" Cgroup="USART" Capiversion="2.4.0" ...>.

title: packchk M379: No example(s) found for Board '[…] …'.
cause: There are no examples found for the board _'BOARD'_. Provide examples. Refer to [/package/examples/example](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_examples_pg.html#element_example).
fix: Add an <example> whose <board name="..." vendor="..."/> matches the board, or pass the pack holding the examples with -i; suppress with -x M379 if the pack has no examples on purpose.

title: packchk M380: No description found for […] '…'
cause: The <description> element that applies to the device (from device, subFamily or family level) is present but empty. Devices have no description attribute; the description is the <description> element.
fix: Write the device text into the <description> element at device, subFamily or family level.
doc_cause: No description was found for the device _'MCU'_ from _'VENDOR'_. Use description attribute to provide information about the device, its subfamily, or family. Refer to [/package/devices/family/.../description](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_description).

message: Vendor names are not equal: '[%VENDOR%] %MCU%', MCU '[%VENDOR2%] %MCU2%', see Line %LINE%
title: packchk M381: Vendor names are not equal: '[…] …', MCU '[…] …', see Line …
cause: The Dvendor of a <mountedDevice> or <compatibleDevice> identifies the device's vendor but is not written the same way as the Dvendor of the device itself (e.g. "ARM" versus "ARM:82"), or it is empty.
fix: Copy the Dvendor value exactly as the device's family defines it, e.g. Dvendor="ARM:82".
doc_cause: Vendor name specified in the Dvendor attribute for the `<mountedDevice>` tag does not match the actual device vendor name. Verify and correct vendor name. Refer to [/package/boards/board/mountedDevice](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_boards_pg.html#element_board_mountedDevice).

message: %TAG% '%NAME%' is not conformant to the pattern "%CHAR%"
title: packchk M383: … '…' is not conformant to the pattern "…"
cause: A device or variant name (Dname or Dvariant) contains characters other than letters, digits, '-', '_' and '/'.
fix: Rename the device or variant using only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '-', '_' (no spaces, dots or parentheses), and update the references to it.
doc_cause: Unsupported characters are found in the _'NAME'_ for the tag/attribute _'TAG'_. Specify the name using only supported characters from _'CHAR'_.

message: Condition '%NAME%': Direct or indirect recursion detected. Skipping condition while searching for '%NAME2%'.
title: packchk M384: Condition '…': Direct or indirect recursion detected. Skipping condition while searching for '…'.
cause: Evaluating a <condition> while collecting the compilers named in the pack's conditions failed: it refers to itself directly or through condition="..." references, or such a reference names a condition id that is not defined. M390 usually reports the same condition earlier.
fix: Follow the condition="..." references from the named condition, break the loop, and define every referenced condition id.

message: Condition '%NAME%': Direct or indirect recursion detected. %MSG%
title: packchk M390: Condition '…': Direct or indirect recursion detected. …
cause: Evaluating a <condition> failed because it refers to itself, directly or through a chain of condition="..." references in its <require>, <accept> or <deny> expressions. The same evaluation error, and so the same message, occurs when such a condition attribute names a condition id that is not defined. packchk skips the condition in later checks.
fix: Follow the condition="..." references from the named condition, break the loop, and make sure every referenced condition id is defined in <conditions>.

title: packchk M398: Attribute 'Dname' missing in expression using 'Pname="…"
cause: When using attribute Pname in the `<condition>` element the Dname attribue shall be present as well. Add attribute token{Dname} specifying the device name. Refer to [/package/conditions/condition](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_conditions_pg.html#element_condition).
fix: Add Dname to the same expression that uses Pname, e.g. <require Dname="MyDevice" Pname="cm4"/>.

title: packchk M505: RTE Model reports: …
cause: Validation of the RTE model built from the loaded PDSC files found an error and prints it as '<pack>: <element> '<id>': error #<n>: <text>'. Typical cases: #501 a component definition with errors such as a condition attribute naming an undefined condition; #502 a condition with an empty expression, mixed B/C/D/T attributes in one expression, or a component expression without Cclass or Cgroup; #503 condition recursion; #530 a device or variant without <processor>; #531 a device property whose Pname names no processor, or an invalid example.
fix: Fix the element named in the message at the reported line (define the condition, split the expression, add Cclass/Cgroup, add the <processor>, correct Pname); the M500 lines that follow give the details.

title: packchk M506: RTE Model reports: …
cause: Validation of the RTE model reported a warning: #500 the same pack (vendor, name, version) is loaded twice, for example because the PDSC under test is also passed with -i; #520 the pack defines a component with the same component ID twice; #521 a condition id is defined more than once (the duplicate is ignored).
fix: Do not pass the checked PDSC, or a second copy of a pack, with -i; make every component definition unique (e.g. a different Cvariant); remove or rename duplicate condition ids.

title: packchk M510: Xerxes reports: …
cause: Xerces reported a warning while validating the PDSC against the PACK.xsd schema; %MSG% is the Xerces text and the line is the PDSC line.
fix: Read the Xerces text and correct the PDSC at that line; make sure the schema in use (--xsd or the installed PACK.xsd) is at least as new as the schemaVersion of the PDSC.

title: packchk M603: No license information found
cause: The PDSC has neither a <license> element nor a <licenseSets> element with at least one <licenseSet>.
fix: Ship the license text in the pack and reference it, e.g. <license>License.txt</license> under <package>, or <licenseSets><licenseSet id="all" default="true"><license name="License.txt" title="BSD-3-Clause"/></licenseSet></licenseSets>.

message: Cannot add Register to group sorter: '%NAME%'
title: svdconv M105: Cannot add Register to group sorter: '…'
cause: While generating the CMSIS device header, svdconv puts all registers and clusters of a peripheral or cluster that start in the same 32-bit word (address with the two low bits cleared) into one union, and that union holds at most 32 members per access size. NAME is the register that did not fit (for 32-bit registers the message already appears from the 31st member on), so far too many registers share one word address, usually through wrong <addressOffset> values or many alternate registers at one address.
fix: Give each register its correct <addressOffset> so that only intended aliases share an address, and keep intentional aliases (<alternateRegister>, <alternateGroup>) at one word address well below 30. The overlap messages M339/M365 name the registers that collide.
note: Only raised with --generate=header. The guard 'regItems > MAX_REGS' lets a 33rd entry be written into a 32-entry array (off by one).

title: svdconv M109: Cannot find '…'
cause: With --generate=sfr on Windows, svdconv looks for SfrCC2.exe in the directory of svdconv.exe and did not find it at the path shown. This is the only place svdconv raises M109.
fix: Put SfrCC2.exe (from Keil MDK/uVision) into the same directory as svdconv.exe, or generate --generate=sfd instead, which needs no SfrCC2.

title: svdconv M124: Cannot execute SfrCC2: '…'!
cause: With --generate=sfr on Windows, svdconv could not start SfrCC2.exe (opening the pipe to the command failed); PATH shows the command it tried.
fix: Check that SfrCC2.exe exists next to svdconv.exe and can be started from a command prompt; otherwise use --generate=sfd.

title: svdconv M127: SfrCC2 reports errors!
cause: With --generate=sfr, SfrCC2.exe compiled the generated .sfd file and exited with code 2 or higher, i.e. it found errors. Its own output is printed just before, in the M125 'SfrCC2 report' block.
fix: Read the SfrCC2 report (M125) printed before this message, correct the SVD element that produced the reported .sfd line, and regenerate.

title: svdconv M128: SfrCC2 reports warnings!
cause: With --generate=sfr, SfrCC2.exe compiled the generated .sfd file and exited with code 1, i.e. it reported warnings. Its own output is printed just before, in the M125 'SfrCC2 report' block.
fix: Read the SfrCC2 report (M125) printed before this message and correct the SVD elements it points to; the .sfr file is still produced.

title: svdconv M130: Cannot create file '…'
cause: svdconv could not open an output file (header, partition, SFD or listing) for writing. The file name is built from the output directory and <device><name>; the directory is not writable, an existing file is read-only or locked, or the name is not a valid file name.
fix: Choose a writable output directory with -o, close programs that hold the file open, remove a read-only attribute, and check that <device><name> contains only characters valid in file names.

message: Tag <%TAG%> unknown or not allowed on this level.
title: svdconv M201: Tag <…> unknown or not allowed on this level.
cause: An element is misspelled or placed under a parent that does not accept it, e.g. <headerStructName> inside a <register>, or <protection> inside a <field> or <interrupt>. svdconv ignores the element; only the first 10 unknown tags of a run are reported.
fix: Check the tag spelling (names are case-sensitive) and move the element to a level where CMSIS-SVD.xsd allows it, or delete it. Vendor-specific data belongs in <vendorExtensions> at the end of <device>.
note: The 10-message limit is a static counter (SvdItem.cpp:210, 260); misplaced <protection> is always reported. Tags containing 'dim' are routed to the dim check and give M240 instead.

title: svdconv M205: Tag <…> empty
cause: An element whose value svdconv converts (a number, boolean, access, usage or other token, an enumeratedValue <value>) is present but empty, e.g. <resetValue></resetValue> or <access/>. The element is treated as not set.
fix: Give the element a value, or remove it so the inherited or default value applies.

title: svdconv M206: DerivedFrom not found: '…'
cause: The derivedFrom attribute names an element svdconv cannot find. The source must be of the same kind (peripheral from peripheral, register from register, ...), must appear earlier in the file because derivedFrom is resolved while parsing, and is looked up among the siblings first and otherwise by a dotted path from the peripheral level (PERIPH.REG). The deriving element is dropped.
fix: Correct the spelling (case-sensitive) of the derivedFrom value, move the source element above the deriving one, and use the dotted path (e.g. derivedFrom="TIMER0.CR1") when the source lies in another peripheral or register.
note: NAME is printed with '%' characters removed. For a <dim> source the lookup compares the <name> as written, including %s or [%s] (SvdItem.cpp:450-463).

message: Expression marker found but no <dim> specified: '%NAME%'
title: svdconv M207: Expression marker found but no <dim> specified: '…'
cause: An element without <dim> has %s or a trailing [%s] in its <name>, <displayName> or <description>. These placeholders are expanded only for dim elements, so svdconv drops the element; a literal '%s' in a description triggers it too. NAME shows the text with the placeholder removed.
fix: Add <dim> and <dimIncrement> (and <dimIndex> for a %s list) if the element is meant to repeat; otherwise remove %s / [%s] from the name, displayName and description.

message: Ignoring <dimIndex> because specified <name> requires Array generation.
title: svdconv M208: Ignoring <dimIndex> because specified <name> requires Array generation.
cause: A dim element uses the array form [%s] in its <name> and also has <dimIndex>. Arrays are always indexed 0..dim-1, so svdconv ignores the <dimIndex>.
fix: Remove <dimIndex>, or, if the custom indices are wanted, switch to the list form with %s (e.g. <name>CH%s</name>), which creates separate elements named with the <dimIndex> values.
note: Error under --strict. Not raised for elements that got the dim data through derivedFrom.

message: CPU section not set. This is required for CMSIS Headerfile generation and debug support.
title: svdconv M209: CPU section not set. This is required for CMSIS Headerfile generation and debug support.
cause: The <device> has no <cpu> element. svdconv needs it for the core configuration in the CMSIS header and for the interrupt checks, and debuggers use it; header generation reports M209 again.
fix: Add a <cpu> element to <device> (after <description>/<licenseText>) with the values of the actual core, e.g. <cpu><name>CM4</name><revision>r0p1</revision><endian>little</endian><mpuPresent>true</mpuPresent><fpuPresent>true</fpuPresent><nvicPrioBits>4</nvicPrioBits><vendorSystickConfig>false</vendorSystickConfig></cpu>.

message: Use new Format CMSIS-SVD >= V1.1 and add <CPU> Section.
title: svdconv M210: Use new Format CMSIS-SVD >= V1.1 and add <CPU> Section.
cause: The <device> has schemaVersion="1.0" and no <cpu> element; CMSIS-SVD 1.0 had no <cpu> section.
fix: Set schemaVersion on <device> to 1.1 or later (e.g. schemaVersion="1.3") and add a <cpu> element for the core, e.g. <cpu><name>CM4</name><revision>r0p1</revision><endian>little</endian><mpuPresent>true</mpuPresent><fpuPresent>true</fpuPresent><nvicPrioBits>4</nvicPrioBits><vendorSystickConfig>false</vendorSystickConfig></cpu>.
doc_cause: Update schema and add CPU section.

title: svdconv M213: Expression for '…' incomplete, <…> missing.
cause: An element has dim data but lacks <dim> or <dimIncrement>; both are required as soon as any dim element (<dim>, <dimIncrement>, <dimIndex>, <dimName>) is present. svdconv drops the element.
fix: Add the missing element, e.g. <dim>4</dim> and <dimIncrement>0x4</dimIncrement>, or remove the other dim elements if the element does not repeat.

message: Peripheral '%NAME%' <dim> single-instantiation is not supported (use Array instead).
title: svdconv M214: Peripheral '…' <dim> single-instantiation is not supported (use Array instead).
cause: A <peripheral> with <dim> uses the list form %s in its <name> (e.g. TIMER%s). svdconv supports dim peripherals only as arrays with [%s] at the end of the name, and drops the peripheral.
fix: Use the array form, e.g. <name>TIMER[%s]</name> with <dim> and <dimIncrement> (peripherals take no <dimIndex>), or write each instance as its own <peripheral>, using derivedFrom to share the registers.

message: Size of <dim> is only one element for '%NAME%', is this intended?
title: svdconv M215: Size of <dim> is only one element for '…', is this intended?
cause: An element has <dim>1</dim>, so the array or list has a single instance.
fix: If there is only one instance, remove <dim>, <dimIncrement> and the %s / [%s] placeholder; otherwise set <dim> to the real number of instances.

title: svdconv M216: Unsupported character found in '…' : ….
cause: A <name>, <description>, register <displayName> or enumerated-value name contains a character svdconv does not support: a byte outside printable ASCII 0x20..0x7E (UTF-8 letters such as ä or µ, ©, typographic quotes or dashes, non-breaking spaces; each byte is reported) or a double quote. HEX shows the byte; line breaks and tabs are accepted.
fix: Replace the character with plain ASCII (e.g. 'u' for µ, ' instead of typographic quotes, - instead of an en dash) and remove double quotes from the text.
note: The text is kept unchanged in the model; only the SFD generator later drops such bytes (M516).

title: svdconv M217: Forbidden Trigraph '??…' found in '…'.
cause: A <name>, <description> or register <displayName> contains two question marks followed by another character ('??x'), which a C compiler may read as a trigraph once the text lands in the generated header. svdconv flags any character after '??', not only the nine trigraph characters, and keeps the text unchanged.
fix: Rewrite the text so that '??' is never followed by another character, for example use a single '?' or words such as 'unknown'.

title: svdconv M218: Unsupported ESC sequence found in '…' : ….
cause: A <name>, <description> or register <displayName> contains a backslash followed by a character other than 'n' (e.g. \t, \r, \\ or a Windows path). Only \n is supported in SVD texts.
fix: Remove the backslash, use \n for a line break, and write paths with '/'.

title: svdconv M220: C Code generation warning: …
cause: While generating the CMSIS header, the bit mask computed for a field came out even. That happens when the field width is 0 (for example <bitWidth>0</bitWidth>, or <lsb> exactly one above <msb>) and can also happen for a 64-bit field; svdconv adds the comment 'Even number for MASK detected!' next to the field's _Msk define.
fix: Correct the field's bit position so that it is at least one bit wide, for example <bitRange>[7:4]</bitRange> with the most significant bit first, or a <bitWidth> of 1 or more.
note: The other source of M220 ('Peripheral unaligned address', HeaderData_RegStructure.cpp:753) is unreachable because 'unaligned' is always 0 (line 37). The field check M313 only rejects negative widths, so a zero-width field reaches the generator.

title: svdconv M221: Input filename must end with .svd: '…
cause: The input file's extension is not .svd (case is ignored), e.g. .xml. svdconv takes the text after the last '.' of the full path, so an extensionless file inside a directory with a '.' in its name is reported here too.
fix: Rename the input file to <device name>.svd, matching <device><name>.

title: svdconv M222: Input filename has no extension: '…
cause: Meant for an input file name without extension. In svdconv 30f5e81 it cannot appear: with no '.' anywhere in the absolute path svdconv aborts with a critical M104 exception, and with a '.' in a directory name it reports M221 instead.
fix: Rename the input file to <device name>.svd.
note: Bug: inputFileName.substr(pos) with pos == npos (SvdDevice.cpp:929) throws std::out_of_range before the M222 test runs.

message: Input File Name '%INFILE%' does not match the tag <name> in the <device> section: '%NAME%'
title: svdconv M223: Input File Name '…' does not match the tag <name> in the <device> section: '…'
cause: The SVD file name without path and extension differs from <device><name>; the comparison is case-sensitive (e.g. stm32f4.svd for <name>STM32F4</name>).
fix: Rename the file to exactly <device><name> plus .svd, or change <device><name> to match the file; the generated header is named after <device><name>.
note: Error under --strict.

message: Enumerated Value Container: Only one Item allowed on this Level!
title: svdconv M228: Enumerated Value Container: Only one Item allowed on this Level!
cause: A <peripheral>, <cluster> or <register> contains more than one <dimArrayIndex>; only the first is used and the others are ignored.
fix: Keep one <dimArrayIndex> per array and put all its <enumeratedValue> entries into it.
note: Logged without a line number.

message: Register '%NAME%' is not an array, <dimArrayIndex> is not applicable
title: svdconv M229: Register '…' is not an array, <dimArrayIndex> is not applicable
cause: A <register>, <cluster> or <peripheral> has <dimArrayIndex> but is not an array: it has no <dim>, or its <name> does not end with [%s]. The text always says 'Register', and NAME is the name of the <dimArrayIndex> container (often empty), not of the element.
fix: Make the element an array (<name>X[%s]</name> with <dim> and <dimIncrement>) or remove the <dimArrayIndex>.
