note: For peripherals and clusters M242 or M243 is reported as well.

title: svdconv M230: Value '…:…' out of Range for … '…[…]'.
cause: An <enumeratedValue> in <dimArrayIndex> has a <value> that is not a valid array index: it is greater than or equal to <dim>. svdconv drops that enumeratedValue.
fix: Use values from 0 to dim-1 in <dimArrayIndex>, or raise <dim> if the array has more elements.

message: Tag <%TAG%> name '%NAME%' must not have specifier '%CHAR%'. Ignoring entry.
title: svdconv M232: Tag <…> name '…' must not have specifier '…'. Ignoring entry.
cause: A <peripheral> or <cluster> has a <headerStructName> that contains '%' (e.g. copied from a %s or [%s] name). svdconv ignores the headerStructName.
fix: Use a plain C identifier in <headerStructName>, e.g. <headerStructName>TIMER</headerStructName>, without %s or [%s].

title: svdconv M233: Parse error: <…> = '…'
cause: An <access> value is not one of read-only, write-only, read-write, writeOnce or read-writeOnce (or the deprecated read/write). svdconv treats the access as not set on that element; this is the <access> form of M202.
fix: Use one of the schema tokens in exact spelling, e.g. <access>read-write</access>.
note: Error under --strict.

title: svdconv M234: No valid items found for … '…'
cause: After the checks, a <peripheral> or a <cluster> directly inside a peripheral has no valid register left, because all its registers and clusters were dropped by earlier errors. svdconv then ignores the whole peripheral or cluster.
fix: Fix the errors reported earlier for the registers and clusters inside it; the message goes away once at least one register is valid.
note: Error under --strict. A peripheral with no registers at all gets M328 instead.

title: svdconv M235: … '…' cannot be an array.
cause: A <field> has <dim> and a <name> ending in [%s]. Fields cannot be arrays, so svdconv drops the field.
fix: Use the list form with %s, e.g. <name>EN%s</name> with <dim>, <dimIncrement> as the bit distance and optionally <dimIndex>, which creates fields EN0, EN1, ...

title: svdconv M236: Expression for <…> '…' not allowed.
cause: A <dimName> contains %s. <dimName> is the type name generated for a dim cluster and must be a plain identifier, so svdconv drops the element.
fix: Remove %s from <dimName>, e.g. <dimName>CHANNEL</dimName>.

title: svdconv M237: Nameless … must have <…>.
cause: A <cluster> named just %s (a nameless dim cluster whose instances are named by <dimIndex>) has no <dimName>. svdconv needs <dimName> as the generated type name and drops the cluster.
fix: Add <dimName> to the cluster, e.g. <name>%s</name><dim>2</dim><dimIncrement>0x10</dimIncrement><dimIndex>TX,RX</dimIndex><dimName>CHANNEL</dimName>, or give the cluster a real name such as CH%s.

title: svdconv M239: Dim-ed … '…' must have an expression.
cause: An element has <dim> but its <name> contains no placeholder: neither %s nor [%s] at the end. svdconv cannot name the instances and drops the element; a [%s] that is not at the end of the name is not recognised and also lands here.
fix: Add the placeholder: [%s] at the end for an array (REG[%s]) or %s for a list (CH%s_CTRL); otherwise remove <dim> and <dimIncrement>.
note: Error under --strict.

message: Tag <%TAG%> unknown or not allowed on %LEVEL2%:%LEVEL%.
title: svdconv M240: Tag <…> unknown or not allowed on …:….
cause: A dim element (any tag whose name contains 'dim') is not accepted on this level by svdconv: <dimIndex> or <dimName> on a <peripheral>, <dimName> on a <register>, <dimArrayIndex> on a <field>, or any dim element on an <interrupt>. Misspelled tags containing 'dim' land here too. svdconv drops the parent element.
fix: Remove the element or move it to a level that takes it: peripherals take <dim>, <dimIncrement>, <dimArrayIndex>; clusters also <dimIndex> and <dimName>; registers <dim>, <dimIncrement>, <dimIndex>, <dimArrayIndex>; fields <dim>, <dimIncrement>, <dimIndex>, <dimName>. Check the tag spelling.

title: svdconv M242: … '…' <dimArrayIndex> found, but no <dim>
cause: A <peripheral> or <cluster> has <dimArrayIndex> but no <dim>; svdconv also reports M229.
fix: Make it an array with <dim>, <dimIncrement> and a <name> ending in [%s], or remove the <dimArrayIndex>.

message: %LEVEL% '%NAME%' <dimArrayIndex> found, but <dim> does not describe an array
title: svdconv M243: … '…' <dimArrayIndex> found, but <dim> does not describe an array
cause: A <peripheral> or <cluster> has <dim> and <dimArrayIndex>, but its <name> uses %s instead of ending with [%s], so it is not an array; svdconv also reports M229.
fix: End the <name> with [%s] (e.g. UART[%s]) or remove the <dimArrayIndex>.

message: C Expression: Referenced item '%NAME%' not found from: '%MSG%'
title: svdconv M244: C Expression: Referenced item '…' not found from: '…'
cause: A peripheral's <disableCondition> uses a name svdconv cannot resolve. Each operand is looked up as a path that starts with a peripheral name and goes down through clusters to a register and field (separated by '->' or '.'); NAME is the first part of the path that does not exist and MSG is the expression read so far. The disable condition is then dropped.
fix: Write each operand as a full path to an existing register or field using the <name>s of peripheral, cluster, register and field, for example <disableCondition>DCB->DSCSR->CDS == 0</disableCondition> ('->' must be escaped as '->' in XML). Check the spelling of each part.

message: C Expression: Only one Item allowed!
title: svdconv M246: C Expression: Only one Item allowed!
cause: A peripheral contains more than one <disableCondition>; only one is allowed (the schema also allows at most one) and svdconv ignores the extra one. The message carries no line number or peripheral name.
fix: Keep a single <disableCondition> per peripheral and combine several conditions in it with && or ||.
note: LogMsg("M246") is called without a line number, so the output does not say which peripheral is affected; search the file for <disableCondition>.

message: C Expression: Referenced Object must be Register or Field!
title: svdconv M248: C Expression: Referenced Object must be Register or Field!
cause: A name in a peripheral's <disableCondition> resolves to a peripheral or cluster instead of a register or field, for example 'DCB == 0' or a path that stops at a cluster. Only register and field values can be evaluated, so the disable condition is dropped.
fix: Extend the path down to a register or field, for example DCB->DSCSR->CDS == 0 or DCB->DSCSR_Clust->DSCSR->CDS == 0 (with '->' escaped as '->' in XML).

message: Dimension '%NAME%' has an invalid or overflowing index/address range.
title: svdconv M250: Dimension '…' has an invalid or overflowing index/address range.
cause: svdconv prints this error when a <dim> element in the SVD file describes an array of registers or peripherals whose index list or address range is invalid or runs past the addressable space; the %NAME% placeholder is the name of the dimensioned element. The exact trigger is not available here, so this is inferred from the message text alone.
fix: Open the SVD file, find the <dim> entry for the named element, and check that <dim> (the number of elements), <dimIncrement> and, if present, <dimIndex> are consistent with each other and do not place the last element beyond the peripheral's address space. Correct the values and rerun svdconv.
note: Trigger lines were not available; the cause and fix are inferred from the message wording and should be checked against the source. The README documents this message, but its text was not provided here.
doc_cause: Correct the dimension range or increment.

title: svdconv M301: Interrupt number '… : …' already defined: … …
cause: Two <interrupt> elements have the same <value> (interrupt number) but different <name>s; interrupt numbers are unique across the whole device. The first definition (at LINE) is kept and the second is not used.
fix: Give each interrupt its correct <value>. If two peripherals really share one interrupt line, use the same <name> and <value> in both, which svdconv accepts (it only notes this with the low-level warning M304).

message: Size of Register '%NAME%:%NUM%' must be 8, 16 or 32 Bits
title: svdconv M302: Size of Register '…:…' must be 8, 16 or 32 Bits
cause: A register's own <size> is not a width svdconv supports. The code accepts 8, 16, 24, 32 and 64 bits although the message names only 8, 16 and 32, and the register is dropped even though the message is a warning (an error with --strict).
fix: Set the register's <size> to its access width, normally 8, 16 or 32 on Cortex-M devices. A register with fewer implemented bits still uses the full access width and simply has fields only for the implemented bits.
note: Message text is incomplete: 24 and 64 are accepted too.

message: Name not C compliant: '%NAME%' : %HEX%, replaced by '_'
title: svdconv M305: Name not C compliant: '…' : …, replaced by '_'
cause: A <name> contains a character that is not allowed in a C identifier: space, backslash, ':', ';', '.', ',', '#', '?', '(', ')', '+', '-', '*' or '/'. svdconv replaces each such character with '_' (one message per character) and continues with the changed name; names of <enumeratedValue>s are not checked this way.
fix: Use only letters, digits and '_' in <name> (the dim placeholder %s is fine), and put human-readable text into <description> or, for registers, <displayName>.

title: svdconv M306: Schema Version not set for <device>.
cause: The root <device> element has no schemaVersion attribute, which the SVD schema requires to tell which SVD version the file follows. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Add the attribute to the root element, for example <device schemaVersion="1.3">.

title: svdconv M309: Field '…': Offset error: …
cause: A field's bit offset (from <bitOffset>, <lsb> or <bitRange>) is above 63, the highest bit svdconv handles. The field is dropped.
fix: Give the field's position relative to bit 0 of its own register, for example <bitRange>[7:4]</bitRange> or <bitOffset>4</bitOffset><bitWidth>4</bitWidth>; a field always lies inside the register's <size>.

title: svdconv M310: Field '…': BitWidth error: …
cause: A field's width (from <bitWidth>, or <msb> - <lsb> + 1) is more than 64 bits. The field is dropped.
fix: Set the field's <bitWidth> (or <lsb>/<msb>, <bitRange>) to the real width of the bit field; it must fit into its register's <size>.

title: svdconv M311: Field '…': Calculation: MSB or LSB == -1
cause: A field has no complete bit position: none of <bitRange>, the pair <lsb>+<msb> or the pair <bitOffset>+<bitWidth> is given in full (for example only <lsb>, or <bitOffset> without <bitWidth>). The text speaks of MSB or LSB == -1 whichever style is used. The field is dropped.
fix: Give the field one complete bit position, for example <bitRange>[7:4]</bitRange>, or <lsb>4</lsb><msb>7</msb>, or <bitOffset>4</bitOffset><bitWidth>4</bitWidth>. svdconv needs <bitWidth> together with <bitOffset> although the schema marks it optional.
note: Misleading text: it is raised whenever offset or width is missing, not only for <lsb>/<msb>.

title: svdconv M312: Address Block missing for Peripheral '…'
cause: A peripheral has no <addressBlock>, neither its own nor one inherited through derivedFrom. Without it svdconv cannot check that the registers lie in the peripheral's address range (M344) or that peripherals do not overlap (M352); the peripheral itself is kept.
fix: Add an address block that covers the peripheral's registers, for example <addressBlock><offset>0x0</offset><size>0x400</size><usage>registers</usage></addressBlock>.

message: Field '%NAME%': LSB > MSB: BitWith calculates to %NUM%
title: svdconv M313: Field '…': LSB > MSB: BitWith calculates to …
cause: A field's <lsb> is more than one above its <msb> (or a <bitRange> is written with the low bit first), so the computed width msb - lsb + 1 is negative. The field is dropped.
fix: Write the most significant bit first: <bitRange>[7:4]</bitRange>, or <lsb>4</lsb><msb>7</msb>.
note: If <lsb> is exactly <msb>+1 the width is 0 and M313 is not raised; the header generator then warns with M220. 'BitWith' in the text is a typo.

title: svdconv M316: … <name> not set.
cause: An element that needs a name has no <name> or an empty one; LEVEL says which (device, peripheral, cluster, register, field, enumeratedValue, cpu or interrupt). Registers, clusters and fields that are dim lists are exempt. The element is dropped.
fix: Add a <name> that is a C identifier to the element at the reported line, for example <name>CTRL</name>.

title: svdconv M322: … … '…' is meaningless text. Deleted.
cause: An element's <description> is the placeholder text 'no description available' (in any case). svdconv deletes the description. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Write a real description of the element, or leave <description> out.

message: Field '%NAME%' %BITRANGE% does not fit into Register '%NAME2%:%NUM%' %LINE%
title: svdconv M324: Field '…' … does not fit into Register '…:…' …
cause: A field's bit range does not fit into its register: the field is wider than the register's effective <size>, or bit offset + width goes beyond it; LINE is the register's line. The field is dropped. M345 reports the same condition from the register's own check, and M324 appears for fields that check did not reach.
fix: Correct the field's bit position (<bitRange>, <lsb>/<msb> or <bitOffset>/<bitWidth>) or the register's <size>, which may be inherited from the peripheral or device, so that every field lies within bits 0 to size-1.

title: svdconv M328: … '…' has no Registers, ignoring ….
cause: A peripheral or cluster (LEVEL) contains no registers or clusters, and no derivedFrom source supplies any. svdconv drops the element.
fix: Add the registers to the peripheral's <registers> or into the <cluster>, derive the element from one that has them (derivedFrom="NAME"), or remove the empty element.

title: svdconv M333: Duplicate <enumeratedValue> …: '…' (…), already used by '…' (…) …
cause: Two <enumeratedValue>s in the same <enumeratedValues> container of a field have the same <value>; USAGE shows the container's usage. The later one is dropped. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Give each enumeratedValue in a container a distinct <value>, or delete the duplicate. If a value means something different on read and on write, use two containers, one with <usage>read</usage> and one with <usage>write</usage>.

message: Value '%NAME%:%NUM%' does not fit into field '%NAME2%' %BITRANGE%.
title: svdconv M335: Value '…:…' does not fit into field '…' ….
cause: An <enumeratedValue>'s <value> is larger than the largest number the field can hold (2^width - 1). The enumerated value is dropped. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Correct the <value> or the field's width. The value is the raw content of the field, not shifted to the field's bit position in the register.

title: svdconv M337: … '…' already defined …
cause: Two <enumeratedValue>s in the same <enumeratedValues> container have the same <name>; this applies to field enumerations and to the <dimArrayIndex> enumeration of a register, cluster or peripheral array. The later one is dropped. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Give each enumeratedValue in a container a unique <name>, or delete the duplicate.

title: svdconv M338: Field '…' … (…) overlaps '…' … (…) …
cause: Two fields of one register share at least one bit. svdconv checks the read view and the write view separately: a read-only field and a write-only field may overlap, but two fields that are both readable or both writable may not (fields without <access> count as read-write). The later field is dropped.
fix: Correct the bit ranges so the fields do not overlap. If the same bits mean different things on read and on write, describe them as two fields with <access>read-only</access> and <access>write-only</access>.

message: Register '%NAME%' (%ACCESS%) (@%ADDRSIZE%) has same address or overlaps '%NAME2%' (%ACCESS2%) (@%ADDRSIZE2%) %LINE%
title: svdconv M339: Register '…' (…) (@…) has same address or overlaps '…' (…) (@…) …
cause: Two registers placed directly in a peripheral start at the same address with the same access, and the later one has neither an <alternateRegister> naming the other nor an <alternateGroup>. A read-only and a write-only register may share an address; overlaps inside clusters or dim arrays, partial overlaps and overlaps between registers of different access are reported as warning M365 instead.
fix: If the address is wrong, correct the later register's <addressOffset>. If both registers are views of the same address, add <alternateRegister>NAME2</alternateRegister> (the register named in the message) or an <alternateGroup> to the later register.

title: svdconv M340: No Devices found.
cause: The input has no <device> root element: the root element has another name, or the XML could not be parsed at all (then XML errors and M111 'Reading SVD File failed' come first).
fix: Pass an SVD file whose root element is <device schemaVersion="1.3">, and repair any XML syntax errors reported before this message.

title: svdconv M343: … '…' (@…) has same address as '…' …
cause: Two peripherals have the same base address, and the later one has no <alternatePeripheral> naming a peripheral already at that address. If it has an <alternatePeripheral> that names none of them, M348 is printed first.
fix: Correct the later peripheral's <baseAddress>. If it really is another view of the same hardware, add <alternatePeripheral>NAME2</alternatePeripheral> to it, naming the peripheral given in the message.

message: Register '%NAME%' (@%ADDRSIZE%) is outside or does not fit any <addressBlock> specified for Peripheral '%NAME2%' %TEXT%
title: svdconv M344: Register '…' (@…) is outside or does not fit any <addressBlock> specified for Peripheral '…' …
cause: A register's byte range (its offset in the peripheral, cluster offsets included, plus <size>/8) does not lie completely inside any of the peripheral's <addressBlock>s with <usage>registers</usage>; blocks with usage buffer or reserved do not count. TEXT lists the register's range and every address block. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Extend an address block, or add one with <usage>registers</usage>, so that it covers the register; or correct the register's <addressOffset> or <size> if the register is misplaced.

message: Field '%NAME%' %BITRANGE% does not fit into Register '%NAME2%:%NUM%'
title: svdconv M345: Field '…' … does not fit into Register '…:…'
cause: A field's bit offset plus width exceeds the register's effective <size> (which may be inherited from the peripheral or device), so the field does not fit into its register. The field is dropped.
fix: Correct the field's bit position (<bitRange>, <lsb>/<msb> or <bitOffset>/<bitWidth>) or the register's <size> so that every field lies within bits 0 to size-1.

message: Alternate %LEVEL% '%NAME%' does not exist at %LEVEL% address (@%ADDR%)
title: svdconv M348: Alternate … '…' does not exist at … address (@…)
cause: A peripheral with <alternatePeripheral>, or a register with <alternateRegister>, shares its address with another element, but no element at that address has the name given. svdconv then also reports the overlap itself (M343 for peripherals, M339 or M365 for registers). Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Set <alternatePeripheral> or <alternateRegister> to the <name> of the element that occupies the same address (shown in the overlap message that follows), or correct the address if the two should not overlap.

title: svdconv M349: Alternate … '…' is equal to … name '…'
cause: An element's <alternatePeripheral>, <alternateCluster> or <alternateRegister> names the element itself. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Set it to the name of the other element that shares the address, or remove it if there is none.

title: svdconv M350: Peripheral '…' (@…) is not 4Byte-aligned.
cause: A peripheral's base address is not a multiple of 4.
fix: Check <baseAddress>; Cortex-M peripherals normally start on a 4-byte boundary. If the address is right, the warning can be accepted.

title: svdconv M352: AddressBlock of Peripheral '…' (@…) … overlaps '…' (@…) … …
cause: An <addressBlock> of one peripheral overlaps an address block of another peripheral (absolute range = <baseAddress> + <offset>, <size> bytes). A peripheral that has an <alternatePeripheral> is not checked from its own side, and pairs where one names the other as alternate are skipped; other overlapping pairs are usually reported once from each side.
fix: Correct the <baseAddress> or the address block's <offset>/<size> so the ranges do not overlap. If one peripheral is an alias of the other, mark it with <alternatePeripheral>.

message: Peripheral group name '%NAME%' should not end with '_'
title: svdconv M353: Peripheral group name '…' should not end with '_'
cause: A peripheral's <groupName> ends with an underscore.
fix: Remove the trailing '_' from <groupName>, for example <groupName>UART</groupName>.

message: Interrupt '%NUM%:%NAME%' specifies a Core Interrupt. Core Interrupts must not be defined, they are set through <cpu><name>.
title: svdconv M354: Interrupt '…:…' specifies a Core Interrupt. Core Interrupts must not be defined, they are set …
cause: An <interrupt> has the name of a Cortex-M core exception (for example NonMaskableInt, HardFault, MemoryManagement, BusFault, UsageFault, SecureFault, SVCall, DebugMonitor, PendSV, SysTick), as provided for the core in <cpu><name>. Core exceptions come from the CPU type and must not be listed; the interrupt is dropped.
fix: Delete <interrupt> entries for core exceptions and list only the device-specific interrupts, numbered from 0.

message: No Interrupts found on pos. 0..15. External (Vendor-)Interrupts possibly defined on position 16+. External Interrupts must start on position 0
title: svdconv M355: No Interrupts found on pos. 0..15. External (Vendor-)Interrupts possibly defined on position 16+. …
cause: No <interrupt> in the device has a <value> below 16. svdconv takes this as a sign that interrupts were numbered by exception number (first device interrupt = 16) instead of from 0.
fix: Number device interrupts from 0, i.e. subtract 16 from exception numbers. If the device really has no interrupt numbered below 16, the message can be ignored.

message: AddressBlock of Peripheral '%NAME%' %TEXT% overlaps AddressBlock %TEXT2% in same peripheral %LINE%
title: svdconv M358: AddressBlock of Peripheral '…' … overlaps AddressBlock … in same peripheral …
cause: Two <addressBlock>s of the same peripheral overlap. svdconv keeps both for compatibility. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Merge the blocks into one, or change their <offset>/<size> so they do not overlap.

title: svdconv M361: … … '…': 'RESERVED' items must not be defined.
cause: An element's <name>, or a register's <displayName>, is 'reserved' (in any case). Reserved space must not be described as an element, so svdconv drops it. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Delete the element. Unused addresses and bits need no description; the header generator fills gaps with reserved members on its own.

title: svdconv M362: … … '…': 'RESERVED' items must not be defined.
cause: An element's <description> is just 'reserved' (in any case), which marks a placeholder for an unused register, field or value. svdconv only warns and keeps the element.
fix: Delete the element if it only describes unused space, or write a description of what it really does.

message: Register '%NAME%' (%ACCESS%) (@%ADDRSIZE%) has same address or overlaps '%NAME2%' (%ACCESS2%) (@%ADDRSIZE2%) %LINE%
title: svdconv M365: Register '…' (…) (@…) has same address or overlaps '…' (…) (@…) …
cause: Two registers occupy the same address or overlapping bytes, and the later one has no matching <alternateRegister> or <alternateGroup>. This warning variant of M339 is used when the clash is not a plain same-address one between top-level registers: one register is in a cluster or a dim array/list, the start addresses differ (partial overlap), or the access types differ (for example read-write against read-only).
fix: Correct <addressOffset> or <size> if the overlap is a mistake. If the registers are intended views of the same address, add <alternateRegister> naming the other register (NAME2 in the message) or an <alternateGroup> to the later register.

title: svdconv M366: Register '…' size (…Bit) is greater than <dimIncrement> * <addressBitsUnits> (…Bit).
cause: In a register array or list (<dim>), the register's <size> is larger than the distance between instances, <dimIncrement> times the device's <addressUnitBits> (the message calls it 'addressBitsUnits'), so consecutive instances would overlap. The register is dropped.
fix: Set <dimIncrement> to the address distance between instances in address units (bytes on Cortex-M), for example <dimIncrement>4</dimIncrement> for 32-bit registers, or correct the register's <size>.
note: The message names 'addressBitsUnits', which is not an SVD element; the schema element is <addressUnitBits> under <device>.

message: Access Type: Field '%NAME%' (%ACCESS%) does not match Register '%NAME2%' (%ACCESS2%)
title: svdconv M367: Access Type: Field '…' (…) does not match Register '…' (…)
cause: A field's effective <access> does not fit its register's effective access: a read-only register may only contain read-only fields, a write-only or writeOnce register only write-only or writeOnce fields, while a read-write register accepts any field access. Access not set at any level counts as read-write.
fix: Make the field's <access> consistent with the register's: correct the field's <access>, or set the register's <access> to read-write when it holds both readable and writable fields.
note: LogMsg("M367", lineNo) passes no names, so the output shows the literal placeholders <NAME>, <ACCESS>, <NAME2>, <ACCESS2>; use the line number to find the field.

title: svdconv M368: … '…' (@…) has same address as '…' …
cause: Two clusters in the same peripheral or cluster start at the same address, and the later one has no <alternateCluster> naming a cluster already at that address.
fix: Correct the later cluster's <addressOffset>, or, if both clusters are alternative views of the same registers, add <alternateCluster>NAME2</alternateCluster> to the later one.

title: svdconv M370: … '…': <offset> not set.
cause: A register has no <addressOffset> (the message calls it <offset>), and no derivedFrom source supplies one. The register is dropped.
fix: Add <addressOffset> with the register's offset from the peripheral's base address or from the enclosing cluster, for example <addressOffset>0x04</addressOffset>.
note: The message names <offset>, but the register element is <addressOffset>.

title: svdconv M371: … '…' <headerStructName> is equal to hierarchical name
cause: A cluster's <headerStructName> equals the name svdconv derives from the hierarchy anyway (the names of peripheral and enclosing clusters joined with '_', for example TIM1_CH). svdconv drops the redundant headerStructName. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Remove <headerStructName> from the cluster, or set it to a different type name if a specific one is wanted.

title: svdconv M372: … <…> '…' already defined …
cause: A name that must be unique across the whole device is used twice; TAG says which: a peripheral <name>, a peripheral or cluster <headerStructName>, a cluster's derived type name, or an <enumeratedValues> <headerEnumName>. An element derived from the first one (derivedFrom) is exempt. The later element is dropped.
fix: Rename one of the two (LINE gives the first), or use derivedFrom when the second element is meant to reuse the first one's definition.

title: svdconv M373: … <…> '…' already defined …
cause: Two registers or clusters at the same level of a peripheral or cluster end up with the same display name. svdconv compares each register's <displayName> and, where a register has none (and for clusters, which have no <displayName>), its <name>; so registers that share a <name> in different <alternateGroup>s collide here even though the name check accepts them.
fix: Give each register at that level a unique <displayName>, or drop a copied <displayName> so the distinct <name> is used. For registers with the same <name> in different <alternateGroup>s, add a distinct <displayName> to each, e.g. <displayName>CTRL_ALT</displayName>. The line in the message points to the first definition.
note: Error under --strict. The name check appends <alternateGroup> to the name (SvdPeripheral.cpp:806-809) but the displayName check does not, so equal names in different alternate groups without explicit <displayName> look like a false positive.

message: Register Array: Register '%NAME%' size (%NUM%Bit) does not match <dimIncrement> (%NUM2%Bit).
title: svdconv M378: Register Array: Register '…' size (…Bit) does not match <dimIncrement> (…Bit).
cause: A register array (a <register> with <dim> and a <name> ending in [%s]) has a <dimIncrement> that is not exactly its size in bytes: svdconv requires dimIncrement*8 to equal the register <size> in bits, because the array is generated as a contiguous C array; the register is dropped. svdconv also raises M378 for a <peripheral> whose <baseAddress> is missing or unparsable, and the text then still speaks of a register array.
fix: Make <dimIncrement> equal to the register size in bytes, e.g. <size>32</size> with <dimIncrement>4</dimIncrement>. If the registers are spaced further apart, use a %s list instead (<name>CH%s</name>) or put the register into a <cluster> array that carries the larger <dimIncrement>. If NAME is a peripheral, give it a valid <baseAddress>.
note: Misleading reuse: SvdPeripheral.cpp:1502 logs M378 (register-array text, NUM/NUM2 unset) for a peripheral without a valid <baseAddress>. M366 is the related check that the increment is not smaller than the register.

message: AddressBlock of Peripheral '%NAME%' (@%ADDR%) %TEXT% does not fit into 32Bit Address Space.
title: svdconv M380: AddressBlock of Peripheral '…' (@…) … does not fit into 32Bit Address Space.
cause: An <addressBlock> of a peripheral ends beyond 0xFFFFFFFF: the peripheral <baseAddress> plus the block's <offset> and <size> - 1 does not fit into 32 bits. svdconv ignores that address block.
fix: Correct the peripheral's <baseAddress> or the address block's <offset> and <size> so the block ends at or below 0xFFFFFFFF; <size> is the length of the block, not its end address.
note: Error under --strict. TEXT prints the range as [end ... start]; ADDR is cast to 32 bits.

message: %LEVEL% '%NAME%': %NAME2% '%HEXNUM%' does not fit into %LEVEL% width: %NUM% Bit.
title: svdconv M382: … '…': … '…' does not fit into … width: … Bit.
cause: A register's <resetValue> or <resetMask> has bits set above the register width (e.g. 0x1FF for an 8-bit register); the width is the register's effective <size>, which may be inherited from the peripheral or device. svdconv replaces the value with 0.
fix: Make <resetValue> and <resetMask> fit the register width, e.g. <resetMask>0xFF</resetMask> for <size>8</size>, or correct the register's <size> if that is what is wrong.
note: Error under --strict. NAME2 says which of the two values failed (Reset Value or Reset Mask).

message: MVE Floating-Point support is set but MVE is not set
title: svdconv M388: MVE Floating-Point support is set but MVE is not set
cause: <cpu> sets <mveFP> to true while <mvePresent> is missing or false; MVE floating point requires MVE.
fix: Add <mvePresent>true</mvePresent> to <cpu> when the core implements MVE with floating point, or set <mveFP> to false (or remove it) for an integer-only or no-MVE configuration.
note: Dead check at 30f5e81: the test (m_mveFP && !m_mvePresent) sits inside if(m_mvePresent), so svdconv never reports M388. mvePresent and mveFP are not in the CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 of CMSIS 5.9.0.

message: SFD Code generation: Unsupported character found in '%NAME%' : %HEX%.
title: svdconv M516: SFD Code generation: Unsupported character found in '…' : ….
cause: During SFD generation (--generate=sfd or sfr) a text contains a character svdconv cannot write into the SFD file: a byte outside printable ASCII 0x20..0x7E (UTF-8 letters, µ, ©, typographic quotes or dashes, each byte reported separately) or a double quote. The description of a peripheral, cluster, register, field, interrupt or enumerated value is checked, falling back to its displayName or name; non-ASCII bytes are dropped and double quotes escaped.
fix: Replace the character in the <description> (or <displayName>/<name> when there is no description) with plain ASCII, e.g. 'u' or 'micro' for µ, ' instead of typographic quotes, - instead of an en dash, and avoid double quotes.
note: Called without a line number (default -1). The same text usually raised M216 in the check phase.

message: SFD Code generation: Forbidden Trigraph '??%CHAR%' found in '%NAME%'.
title: svdconv M517: SFD Code generation: Forbidden Trigraph '??…' found in '…'.
cause: During SFD generation a description contains two question marks followed by another character ('??x'), which a C preprocessor could read as a trigraph. svdconv reports any character after '??', not only the nine trigraph characters, and drops that character.
fix: Remove or reword the '??' in the <description>, e.g. write a single '?' or '(unknown)'.

message: SFD Code generation: Unsupported ESC sequence found in '%NAME%' : %CHAR%.
title: svdconv M518: SFD Code generation: Unsupported ESC sequence found in '…' : ….
cause: During SFD generation a description contains a backslash followed by a character other than 'n' (e.g. \t, \r, \\ or a Windows path). Only \n is supported; svdconv drops the character after the backslash.
fix: Remove the backslash or rewrite the text: use \n for a line break, write paths with '/', and use no other C escape sequences in <description>.
note: Source FIXME (SvdUtils.cpp:1310) notes the conversion mangles such sequences.

message: '<…>' contains non-portable backslash, use forward slash instead
title: csolution: '…' contains non-portable backslash, use forward slash instead
cause: A path value in a csolution.yml, cproject.yml or clayer.yml contains a backslash, for example under projects: project:, layers: layer:, files: file:, add-path:, linker: script:/regions:, packs: path:, output-dirs: or generators:. The `<…>` is the path as written; the message is prefixed with the YAML file, line and column.
fix: Write the path with forward slashes, e.g. `- file: ../src/main.c` instead of `..\src\main.c`; forward slashes work on Windows, Linux and macOS.

title: csolution: '…' has case inconsistency, use '…' instead
cause: A relative path in a csolution.yml, cproject.yml or clayer.yml points to an existing file or folder, but its upper/lower case differs from the name on disk. It only shows on case-insensitive file systems (Windows, default macOS), where the path still resolves; on Linux the same path is not found. The first `<…>` is the path as written, the second the path with the case on disk, relative to the YAML file.
fix: Replace the path with the suggested spelling, e.g. `- layer: ../layer.clayer.yml` instead of `../laYer.clayer.yml`, so the project also builds on case-sensitive hosts such as Linux CI runners.

message: '<…>' is not a valid command. See 'csolution --help'.
title: csolution: '…' is not a valid command. See 'csolution --help'.
cause: `-h`/`--help` was given together with a command or subcommand that csolution does not know, e.g. `csolution list invalid -h` or `csolution test -h`. The `<…>` is the command (and subcommand) as typed.
fix: Run `csolution --help` and use one of the listed commands, e.g. `csolution convert -h` or `csolution list packs -h`. Valid are convert, update-rte, run, rpc, check pack-updates and list with packs, boards, devices, npus, components, configs, dependencies, examples, templates, contexts, targets, target-sets, debuggers, generators, layers, toolchains or environment.

message: '<…>' is not selectable as active target-set
title: csolution: '…' is not selectable as active target-set
cause: The value of `--active`/`-a` (`<target-type>[@<target-set>]`) does not match the csolution.yml: no entry under target-types: has that `type:` name, or that type has no target-set: entry whose `set:` equals the part after `@`. The `<…>` is the value as given.
fix: List the valid values with `csolution list target-sets <name>.csolution.yml` and pass one of them, e.g. `-a CM0` or `-a CM0@Production`; or add the set to the target type (`target-set: - set: Production`). Names are case-sensitive.

message: '<…>' this linker script is ignored<…>; multiple linker scripts defined<…>
title: csolution: '…' this linker script is ignored…; multiple linker scripts defined…
cause: A linker script file (extension .ld, .sct, .scf, .icf, .src or `category: linkerScript`) is listed under groups: files:, but the context's linker script is already decided: by a `linker:` node with `script:`, `regions:`, `define:` or `auto:`, or by an earlier linker script file in the groups. The file named in `<…>` is ignored; the suffix `; multiple linker scripts defined` is added when a script was already set.
fix: Keep one linker script per context: remove the extra file from groups:, or name the one you want with `linker: - script: <file>` and drop the other, or limit the entries with `for-context:`/`for-compiler:`. With `regions:` or `define:` a script listed only in groups: is ignored, so put your own script under `linker: - script:`; with `auto:` remove linker scripts from groups:.

title: csolution: 'for-compiler: …' is not supported
cause: A `for-compiler:` value (on a file, group, setup or linker entry) names a compiler for which no toolchain configuration file `<name>.<version>.cmake` exists in the compiler root (CMSIS_COMPILER_ROOT, default <cmsis-toolbox>/etc). The name match is case-sensitive, so `Ac6` is reported while `AC6` is fine; the `<…>` is the name before `@`.
fix: Spell the compiler as the toolchain files do: AC6, GCC, IAR, CLANG, CLANG_TI or XC, e.g. `for-compiler: AC6@>=6.18.1`. If the spelling is right, check that CMSIS_COMPILER_ROOT points to the CMSIS-Toolbox etc folder that contains the matching *.cmake file.

title: csolution: 'telnet:' pname is required (multicore device)
cause: The device has more than one processor, and an entry under `debugger: telnet:` (target-set in the csolution.yml) has no `pname:`. csolution cannot tell which core the telnet settings belong to and skips the entry.
fix: Add the processor name to each telnet entry, e.g. `telnet: - mode: monitor  pname: cm0_core0  port: 4444`. The pnames are those of the device's processors (the `:<pname>` used in `device:`).

message: <…>'device: Dname'<…>'board:' node<…> is deprecated at this level and accepted in *.csolution.yml only
title: csolution: …'device: Dname'…'board:' node… is deprecated at this level and accepted in *.csolution.yml only
cause: A cproject.yml or clayer.yml sets `device:` with a device name or sets `board:`. Board and device belong to the target-types: of the csolution.yml; in a project or layer only the processor form `device: :<pname>` is accepted without warning.
fix: Move `board:`/`device:` to the target type in the csolution.yml (`target-types: - type: MyTarget  board: Vendor::BoardName`) and keep at most `device: :cm33_core0` in the cproject.yml. A layer that targets a board or device uses `for-board:`/`for-device:` instead.

message: a single context must be specified
title: csolution: a single context must be specified
cause: `csolution run -g <generator>` for a generator defined in a pack (not a globally registered one) ran with more than one selected context, e.g. no `-c` option in a solution with several build or target types. The pack generator runs for exactly one context.
fix: Select one context with `-c`, e.g. `csolution run <name>.csolution.yml -g <generator-id> -c <project>.Debug+<target>`; `csolution list contexts <name>.csolution.yml` shows the names.

message: absolute path '<…>' is not portable, use relative path instead
title: csolution: absolute path '…' is not portable, use relative path instead
cause: A path value in a csolution.yml, cproject.yml or clayer.yml (projects:, layers:, files:, add-path:, linker:, packs: path:, output-dirs:, generators: and similar path nodes) is absolute, e.g. `/home/user/...` or `C:/...`. The `<…>` is that path; the message carries file, line and column.
fix: Write the path relative to the YAML file that contains it (e.g. `../common/inc`), or use an access sequence such as `$SolutionDir()$/common/inc`, so the project works on other machines.

message: access sequence '$Pack(<…>)' must have the format '$Pack(vendor::name)$'
title: csolution: access sequence '$Pack(…)' must have the format '$Pack(vendor::name)$'
cause: A `$Pack(...)$` access sequence in a YAML path or option has an argument without both vendor and pack name separated by `::`, e.g. `$Pack(Wrong.Format)$`. The `<…>` is the argument; the sequence is left unexpanded.
fix: Write the pack as `$Pack(Vendor::Name)$`, e.g. `$Pack(ARM::CMSIS)$/CMSIS/Include`.
note: The message prints the given sequence without its closing '$'.

message: access sequence pack was not loaded: '$Pack(<…>)$'
title: csolution: access sequence pack was not loaded: '$Pack(…)$'
cause: A `$Pack(Vendor::Name)$` access sequence refers to a pack that is not among the packs loaded for the context: it is not listed under packs: of the csolution.yml/cproject.yml/clayer.yml (when packs are listed, only those are loaded) or it is not installed. The `<…>` is the pack as written; the sequence stays unexpanded, so the resulting path is wrong.
fix: Add the pack to packs:, e.g. `- pack: ARM::CMSIS`, and install it with `cpackget add Vendor::Name`; or correct the vendor/name spelling in the `$Pack(...)$` sequence.

title: csolution: board '…' was not found
cause: The `board:` of the target type (format `[Vendor::]Name[:Revision]`) matches no board in the loaded packs: no board has exactly that name, or the vendor before `::` differs. Only boards of the packs listed under packs: are searched (all installed packs when none are listed). The `<…>` is the board as written; the same text is printed when name and vendor match but no board has the given `:Revision`.
fix: Look up the exact name with `csolution list boards <name>.csolution.yml -f <part-of-name>` and copy it into `board:`; if the board is missing there, add its board support pack under packs: and install it with `cpackget add Vendor::PackName`.

message: build-type '.<…>' does not exist in solution<…>, did you mean '+<…>'?<…>
title: csolution: build-type '.…' does not exist in solution…, did you mean '+…'?…
cause: A `for-context:` or `not-for-context:` entry in a csolution.yml, cproject.yml or clayer.yml uses `.Name`, but Name is not a build type defined under build-types: (nor in a context-map:). When Name is a target type, the warning asks whether `+Name` was meant, since `.` marks build types and `+` target types. The same check prints `target-type '+Name' does not exist in solution` for unknown target types.
fix: Correct the filter, e.g. `for-context: .Debug` for a build type or `for-context: +CM3` for a target type, or add the missing type under build-types:/target-types: in the csolution.yml. Names are case-sensitive.

message: cgen file was not found, run generator '<…>' for context '<…>'
title: csolution: cgen file was not found, run generator '…' for context '…'
cause: A selected component uses a globally registered generator (for example STM32CubeMX), and the generator import file `<project-or-name>.cgen.yml` that this generator writes does not exist in its output folder. The generator has not been run for this context yet, or `generators: options:` (`path:`/`name:`) point elsewhere. The first `<…>` is the generator id, the second the context.
fix: Run the generator for the context, e.g. `csolution run <name>.csolution.yml -g <generator-id> -c <context>`, then convert/build again; if it was run, make `generators: options: - generator: <id>  path: ...` point to the folder that holds the .cgen.yml.

message: clayer search path does not exist
title: csolution: clayer search path does not exist
cause: The folder given with `--clayer-path`/`-L` to `csolution list layers` does not exist. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not against the csolution.yml; the message is prefixed with the resolved path.
fix: Pass an existing folder, e.g. `csolution list layers <name>.csolution.yml -L ./layers` from the folder that contains it, or an absolute path.

message: command line options '--quiet' and '--verbose' are mutually exclusive
title: csolution: command line options '--quiet' and '--verbose' are mutually exclusive
cause: Both `--quiet`/`-q` and `--verbose`/`-v` were given on the csolution command line (for example passed through by cbuild); they contradict each other.
fix: Remove one of the two options.

message: component '<…>' does not accept more than <…> instance(s)
title: csolution: component '…' does not accept more than … instance(s)
cause: A component under components: sets `instances:` higher than its pack allows: the pack's maxInstances attribute, or 1 when the pack does not set it. The `<…>` are the component and the allowed maximum.
fix: Lower `instances:` to the maximum or remove it (one instance is the default), or select a component variant that supports several instances.

message:
component '<…>' not found in included packs<…>
  did you mean '<…>'?<…>
title: csolution: component '…' not found in included packs… did you mean '…'?…
cause: A `component:` entry matches no component that the loaded packs offer for this context. Either the pack is not listed under packs:/not installed, the ID is misspelled or incomplete (Cclass:Cgroup:Csub, `&Cvariant`, vendor `::`), the version after `@` matches no available version, or the component's pack condition excludes the device, board or compiler. When exactly one component matches partially, the message adds `did you mean '<id>'`.
fix: Use the suggested ID if one is shown; otherwise run `csolution list components <name>.csolution.yml -c <context>` to see what is available and copy the ID, and add the missing pack under packs: (then `cpackget add Vendor::PackName`).

message: conflict: automatic linker script generation overrules specified script '<…>'
title: csolution: conflict: automatic linker script generation overrules specified script '…'
cause: The context has `linker: - auto:` and also a linker script from `linker: - script:` (in the cproject.yml, a clayer.yml or a setup). Automatic linker script generation wins and the named script, shown in `<…>`, is dropped.
fix: Keep one of the two: remove `auto:` to use your script, or remove `script:` to use the generated one; or restrict either entry with `for-context:`/`for-compiler:`.

message: conflict: component '<…>' is listed multiple times
title: csolution: conflict: component '…' is listed multiple times
cause: The same `component:` string appears more than once under components: of the cproject.yml for the same context (entries are compared as written, after for-context:/not-for-context: filtering). The same duplicate coming from a clayer.yml only gives the warning 'ignoring conflict'.
fix: Delete the duplicate entry, or give the entries disjoint `for-context:` filters if they belong to different build or target types.

message: conflict: group '<…>' is declared multiple times
title: csolution: conflict: group '…' is declared multiple times
cause: Two groups with the same `group:` name sit at the same level for one context. Top-level groups of the cproject.yml, of all its clayer.yml files and of a generator's *.cgen.yml are merged into one list, so a name used in the project and in a layer or generated file collides; nested groups are compared within their parent group.
fix: Rename one of the groups (e.g. `group: App Sources` vs `group: Board Sources`), or give them disjoint `for-context:` filters.

message: context '<…>' generator '<…>' from component '<…>': gpdsc validation failed
title: csolution: context '…' generator '…' from component '…': gpdsc validation failed
cause: The gpdsc file that a pack generator wrote for a component (its path prefixes the message) loads, but fails pack validation without a specific error, e.g. a component in it references a condition that does not exist. csolution still uses the file. The `<…>` are the context, the generator id and the component that started the generator.
fix: Re-run the generator so it writes a fresh gpdsc: `csolution run <name>.csolution.yml -g <generator-id> -c <context>`. If the warning stays, the generator or its pack produces an inconsistent gpdsc; update them or report it to their vendor.

message: context '<…>' generator '<…>' from component '<…>': reading gpdsc failed
title: csolution: context '…' generator '…' from component '…': reading gpdsc failed
cause: A selected component is handled by a generator defined in its pack, and the generator's gpdsc file (its path prefixes the message) cannot be loaded: it does not exist yet because the generator has not been run for this context, or it is not valid XML/PDSC. The `<…>` are the context, the generator id and the component; RTE parser errors with details may follow.
fix: Run the generator for the context: `csolution run <name>.csolution.yml -g <generator-id> -c <context>` (`csolution list generators <name>.csolution.yml -c <context>` shows the ids). If the file exists, regenerate it or fix the XML error reported after this message.

message: context '<…>' referenced by access sequence '<…>' does not exist or is not selected
title: csolution: context '…' referenced by access sequence '…' does not exist or is not selected
cause: An access sequence with a context argument in a cproject.yml or clayer.yml, such as `$elf(project.Debug+Target)$`, `$cmse-lib(...)$`, `$OutDir(...)$` or `$ProjectDir(...)$`, refers to a context that is not among the contexts selected for this run: the project, build type or target type is misspelled, or that context is excluded by `-c`, `--active` or the cbuild-set. Omitted project or target parts default to those of the current context. The `<…>` are the referenced context and the sequence name.
fix: Correct the context name in the access sequence (`csolution list contexts <name>.csolution.yml` lists them) and make sure the referenced context is built in the same run, e.g. select it with an additional `-c <context>` or add it to the target-set.

message: context '<…>' referenced by access sequence '<…>' is not compatible
title: csolution: context '…' referenced by access sequence '…' is not compatible
cause: A solution-level node of the csolution.yml (for example `executes:` input/output) uses an access sequence such as `$elf(unknown.Debug+Target)$` whose context argument matches no context of the solution: no context name contains the given text. Despite the wording, it means the context was not found. The `<…>` are the context text and the sequence name.
fix: Correct the context name in the access sequence to an existing `<project>.<build-type>+<target-type>` (see `csolution list contexts <name>.csolution.yml`).
note: 'is not compatible' is misleading: the check is a substring match over all context names.

title: csolution: cproject file was not found
cause: A `project:` entry under projects: in the csolution.yml names a cproject.yml that does not exist at that path, relative to the folder of the csolution.yml. The message is prefixed with the path as written.
fix: Correct the path and file name (case matters on Linux), e.g. `- project: app/app.cproject.yml`, or create the missing project file.

title: csolution: cproject.yml filenames must be unique
cause: Two entries under projects: of the csolution.yml use the same cproject file name in different folders, e.g. app1/app.cproject.yml and app2/app.cproject.yml. The project name, and with it the context names, is taken from the file name, so the names must differ.
fix: Rename one of the project files, e.g. app2/app2.cproject.yml, and update its `project:` entry.

message: cproject.yml files should be placed in separate sub-directories
title: csolution: cproject.yml files should be placed in separate sub-directories
cause: Two or more projects under projects: of the csolution.yml are in the same folder. Projects in one folder share that folder's RTE directory and other per-project outputs.
fix: Give each cproject.yml (with its sources) its own folder, e.g. app/app.cproject.yml and boot/boot.cproject.yml, and update the `project:` paths.

title: csolution: csolution file not specified
cause: The command needs a solution, but none was given: no `--solution`/`-s` option and no positional argument whose name ends in `.csolution.yml` or `.csolution.yaml`. A file with another name is not recognized as the solution.
fix: Pass the solution file, e.g. `csolution convert my.csolution.yml` or `csolution list configs -s my.csolution.yml`; rename the file to `<name>.csolution.yml` if needed.

title: csolution: csolution file was not found
cause: The *.csolution.yml given on the command line (positional or `--solution`/`-s`) does not exist at that path; a relative path is resolved from the current working directory. The message is prefixed with the path as given.
fix: Correct the path or file name, or run csolution from the folder that contains the solution.

title: csolution: destination directory cannot be created
cause: csolution cannot create the folder for a YAML file it writes (cbuild-idx.yml, cbuild.yml, cbuild-pack.yml, cbuild-run.yml, cbuild-gen.yml and similar), e.g. because a plain file exists where a folder of the path is needed or the location is not writable. The message is prefixed with the file path.
fix: Remove or rename the file that blocks the path (e.g. a file named `tmp` or `out` in the solution folder), make the location writable, or choose another output folder with `--output`/`-o` or output-dirs:.

title: csolution: device '…' does not support '…: …'
cause: The `processor:` node (in a target type or build type of the csolution.yml, or in the cproject.yml) asks for a feature the selected device or core does not have: an `endian:` the device does not use, `fpu: dp` on a single-precision FPU, or `fpu`, `dsp`, `mve`, `trustzone` or `branch-protection` on a device without that feature. The `<…>` are the device and the `key: value` asked for.
fix: Remove the setting, or set it to `off` where the key allows it (e.g. `processor: trustzone: off`; `endian:` has no off), or select a device or processor that has the feature.

message: file '<…>.base' not found; base version unknown
title: csolution: file '….base' not found; base version unknown
cause: A component configuration file in the RTE folder exists, but its backup `<file>.base@<version>` beside it is missing, so csolution cannot tell from which pack version the file was copied (PLM status 'missing base'). Typical when the RTE files were last processed with `--no-update-rte`, by an older tool, or the `*.base@*` files were not committed to version control. The `<…>` is the config file path.
fix: Run csolution with RTE update enabled (`csolution update-rte <name>.csolution.yml`, or convert without `--no-update-rte`); it recreates the base backup where it can. Keep the `*.base@*` files under version control together with the RTE folder.

title: csolution: file cannot be written
cause: csolution cannot save an output file whose path prefixes the message, e.g. a folder with the same name exists at that path or the location is not writable. From ProjMgr.cpp:802 it is the legacy `<context>.cprj` written with `--cbuildgen`; the same text is printed for YAML outputs such as *.cbuild.yml.
fix: Remove the folder or file that blocks the path, make the output location writable, or choose another output folder with `--output`/`-o`.

message: file is missing and required due to use of --frozen-packs option
title: csolution: file is missing and required due to use of --frozen-packs option
cause: `--frozen-packs` was given, but the pack lock file `<name>.cbuild-pack.yml` next to the csolution.yml does not exist; frozen packs require it. The message is prefixed with the expected file path.
fix: Run once without `--frozen-packs` to create the cbuild-pack.yml, commit it, and use `--frozen-packs` afterwards (e.g. in CI).

message: file not allowed to be updated
title: csolution: file not allowed to be updated
cause: `--frozen-packs` was given, and the packs csolution resolves for the solution differ from those locked in `<name>.cbuild-pack.yml` (e.g. a pack was added to or removed from packs:, or a version requirement changed), so the lock file would have to change. The message is prefixed with the cbuild-pack.yml path.
fix: Run once without `--frozen-packs` to update the cbuild-pack.yml and commit it, or change packs: back so that it matches the locked list.

title: csolution: found multiple device variants
cause: The selected device, from `device:` or from the board's mounted device, has variants in its pack, and csolution needs one variant. The error that follows lists the variant names.
fix: Set `device:` in the target type to one of the listed variants, e.g. `device: RteTest_ARMCM4_FP`.

title: csolution: found no mounted device
cause: The `board:` refers to a board whose pack description lists no mounted device (only compatible devices). The check fails even when `device:` is also set.
fix: Use a board (or board support pack version) that declares its mounted device, or select the target with `device:` only and drop `board:`.

title: csolution: generator '…' is not dry-run capable
cause: `csolution run --dry-run` was used with a pack generator whose `<exe>` in the pack declares no `<argument mode="dry-run">`, so it cannot run without writing files. The `<…>` is the generator id.
fix: Run the generator without `--dry-run`, or use a generator/pack version that supports dry-run.
note: ExecuteGenerator passes the executable path as the host type to IsDryRunCapable, so a dry-run argument restricted with a host attribute is never recognized.

message: generator '<…>' required by component '<…>' was not found in global register
title: csolution: generator '…' required by component '…' was not found in global register
cause: A selected component names a generator that its pack does not define and that is not registered globally: no *.generator.yml in the CMSIS-Toolbox etc folder has an entry with that `id:`. Typical for components that rely on an external tool such as STM32CubeMX when the installation lacks its registration file. The `<…>` are the generator id and the component.
fix: Use a CMSIS-Toolbox installation whose etc folder contains the generator's *.generator.yml (an entry `generator: - id: <id>  run: ...  path: ...`), or remove the component that needs it.

message: generator file '<…>' cannot be executed, check permissions
title: csolution: generator file '…' cannot be executed, check permissions
cause: The pack generator's executable exists but is not executable for the current user, e.g. a script in the pack without its execute bit after unpacking on Linux/macOS. The `<…>` is the file path. The cbuild-gen.yml input file has already been written at this point.
fix: Make the file executable, e.g. `chmod +x "<path>"`, or reinstall the pack; then run the generator again.

message: generator output directory was not set
title: csolution: generator output directory was not set
cause: A selected component uses a globally registered generator, and no output folder is known for it: no `generators: options: - generator: <id>  path:` and no `generators: base-dir:` in the clayer.yml, cproject.yml or csolution.yml, and no `path:` in the generator's global registration (*.generator.yml).
fix: Set the folder in the cproject.yml (or csolution.yml), e.g. `generators: options: - generator: CubeMX  path: ./CubeMX`, or set `generators: base-dir: ./generated`.

message: ignoring conflict: component '<…>' is listed multiple times
title: csolution: ignoring conflict: component '…' is listed multiple times
cause: A component that is already listed for the context (in the cproject.yml or an earlier processed clayer.yml) is listed again in a clayer.yml. csolution keeps the first entry and drops the layer's duplicate, including any settings on it (define:, misc:, instances: and so on).
fix: Remove the duplicate from either the project or the layer, keeping the entry whose settings should apply.

title: csolution: input csolution.yml was not specified
cause: `csolution check pack-updates` was run without a solution file. The command needs the *.csolution.yml either with `-s`/`--solution` or as a positional argument whose name ends in `.csolution.yml` (or `.csolution.yaml`); a file with any other name is not recognised as the solution.
fix: Pass the solution file: `csolution check pack-updates my.csolution.yml` or `csolution check pack-updates -s path/to/my.csolution.yml`. Rename the file to `<name>.csolution.yml` if it does not follow that pattern.

message: invalid arguments: '-a' option cannot be used in combination with '-S'
title: csolution: invalid arguments: '-a' option cannot be used in combination with '-S'
cause: The command line contains both `-a`/`--active` (select a target-type and target-set) and `-S`/`--context-set` (take the context selection from the <solution>.cbuild-set.yml). Both select the contexts to process, so csolution rejects the combination.
fix: Use only one of them: `-a <target-type>[@<target-set>]` to select by target, or `-S` to reuse the selection stored in the cbuild-set.yml.

title: csolution: invalid define: …, improper quotes
cause: An entry under `define:`, `define-asm:`, `west-defs:` or `linker:` - `define:` has a value with misplaced double quotes; `<…>` is that value. csolution accepts a value with no `"` at all, or one quoted completely: exactly two quotes, either as `"..."` at both ends or as escaped `\"...\"` at both ends. A quote in the middle, a missing closing quote or a mix of `"` and `\"` is rejected. Quotes that are YAML syntax (`- KEY: "value"`) are removed by YAML and do not count.
fix: Quote the whole value or not at all. To pass a C string literal write the escaped form, e.g. `- KEY3: \"valid\"` or `- \"Test 3\"`; for a plain token write `- KEY: value`.

title: csolution: invalid pattern '…': …
cause: A `for-context:` or `not-for-context:` entry starts with `^` or `\`, so csolution treats it as a regular expression, but the expression does not compile; the first `<…>` is the entry, the second the regex library's error text. Example: `for-context: ^.Debug+(CM0` has an unclosed parenthesis.
fix: Correct the regular expression, escaping the literal `.` and `+` of context names, e.g. `for-context: ^\.Debug\+(CM0|CM3)`. If no pattern is meant, use the plain form `.Debug+CM0` without a leading `^` or `\`.

title: csolution: key '…' was not recognized
cause: A YAML file csolution reads (csolution.yml, cproject.yml, clayer.yml, cdefault.yml, cbuild-pack.yml or cbuild-set.yml) contains a key that is not valid at that place; `<…>` is the key and the message carries its file, line and column. It is usually a typo or a key placed under the wrong parent. With the schema check on, the schema normally reports the key first; this warning is what remains with `-n`/`--no-check-schema` or when the schemas are not installed.
fix: Fix the spelling or move the key to the node where the YAML schema allows it (schemas/*.schema.json), or remove it. Run without `-n` to get the schema's report on the same line.

message: linker script template for compiler '<…>' was not found
title: csolution: linker script template for compiler '…' was not found
cause: The project has no linker script of its own (no `linker:` - `script:` in cproject.yml or clayer.yml and none from a component), or uses `linker:` - `auto:`, so csolution looks for the template `<compiler>_linker_script.*` of the selected compiler; `<…>` is that compiler. It searches the compiler root (environment variable CMSIS_COMPILER_ROOT, otherwise the `etc` folder of the CMSIS-Toolbox installation) and found no template there. Templates exist for AC6, GCC, IAR, CLANG, CLANG_TI and XC. The context then has no linker script.
fix: Check that CMSIS_COMPILER_ROOT points to the toolbox's `etc` folder, or that the CMSIS-Toolbox installation is complete, and that `compiler:` names a supported toolchain. Alternatively give the project its own script: `linker:` - `script: path/to/file.sct` in the cproject.yml.

message: loaded pack '<…>' does not match specified metadata '<…>'
title: csolution: loaded pack '…' does not match specified metadata '…'
cause: A `packs:` entry pins a version with build metadata, such as `- pack: ARM::RteTest_DFP@0.1.1+user_metadata`, but the installed pack of that version carries different metadata after the `+` in its release version. The first `<…>` is the loaded pack (printed without the `@` before the version), the second the metadata from the YAML. The pack is still used.
fix: Make the `+<metadata>` suffix in the `packs:` entry match the installed pack, or drop the suffix: `- pack: ARM::RteTest_DFP@0.1.1`.

title: csolution: manifest file does not exist
cause: The csolution.yml has `created-for: CMSIS-Toolbox@<version>`, and to compare versions csolution looks for `manifest_<x.y.z>*.yml` in the CMSIS-Toolbox installation directory (the parent of the folder that holds the csolution executable). No such file is there, so the minimum-version check is skipped.
fix: Use csolution from a complete CMSIS-Toolbox installation, whose root folder contains the manifest file; reinstall the toolbox if it is missing. The warning does not stop the run.

title: csolution: missing device and/or board info
cause: The context has neither a `board:` nor a device name in `device:` at any level (target-types in the csolution.yml, the cproject.yml or a clayer.yml). A `device:` with only a processor name, such as `device: :cm0_core0`, does not count.
fix: Add a board or a device to the target type in the csolution.yml, e.g. `target-types:` - `type: CM0` with `device: ARMCM0` or `board: <vendor>::<board name>`.

message: mlops.npu.macs value does not match DFP device information
title: csolution: mlops.npu.macs value does not match DFP device information
cause: `mlops:` - `npu:` - `macs:` in the csolution.yml (possibly combined with `npu: type:`) names a MAC count that no NPU of the selected device offers. csolution compares it with the `<feature type="NPU">` entries the DFP declares for the processors of the MLOps contexts; a type and a MAC count that each exist but not on the same NPU also trigger it. The value is still used for the Vela options.
fix: Set `macs:` to a value the device supports, or leave `npu:` out so that csolution takes type and MACs of the first NPU in the DFP. `csolution list npus my.csolution.yml` shows the NPUs and MAC counts per device.

message: mlops: <…>no default unnamed target set for '<…>'<…>target set '<…>' not found<…>
title: csolution: mlops: …no default unnamed target set for '…'…target set '…' not found…
cause: `mlops:` - `hardware:` or `simulator:` - `target:` names a target type whose target sets do not contain the requested one. Without `@<set>` (e.g. `target: Hardware`) csolution needs a `target-set:` entry with an empty `set:` name and reports `no default unnamed target set for '<type>'`; with `target: <type>@<set>` it reports `target set '<type>@<set>' not found` when no entry has that `set:` name.
fix: Name an existing set in `target: <type>@<set>`, or add the set under the target type in the csolution.yml: `target-set:` - `set: <set>` (an entry with an empty `set:` serves as the default).

message: mlops: no image or project-context specified for target '<…>'
title: csolution: mlops: no image or project-context specified for target '…'
cause: `mlops:` - `hardware:` or `simulator:` - `target:` selects a target set whose `images:` list has no `project-context:` that names a project of the solution, so there is no context to build or run for that target. `<…>` is the target. Example: `images:` - `project-context: wrong_context`.
fix: In that target set add or correct an `images:` entry so that `project-context:` names a project from `projects:` in the csolution.yml, e.g. `- project-context: core0`.

title: csolution: mlops: target type '…' not found
cause: `mlops:` - `hardware:` or `simulator:` - `target:` names a target type that is not declared under `target-types:` in the csolution.yml; `<…>` is that name (the part before `@`).
fix: Use the `type:` of an existing target type in `target: <type>[@<set>]`, or add that target type under `target-types:`.

message: more than one valid <serialwire> element found
title: csolution: more than one valid <serialwire> element found
cause: The device description in the DFP has more than one `<serialwire>` element in its `<trace>` sections that apply to the whole device (trace elements with a Pname attribute are ignored). csolution writes only one serial-wire trace sink into the cbuild-run.yml. It is a flaw of the pack, not of the project.
fix: Nothing to change in the project; the run and debug files are still written. Report the duplicate `<serialwire>` to the DFP vendor or update to a DFP version that fixes it.

message: no compatible software layer found. Review required connections of the project
title: csolution: no compatible software layer found. Review required connections of the project
cause: `csolution list layers` could not complete layer discovery for the context named with the message. Mostly no combination of clayer.yml files (from the loaded packs or from `-L`/`--clayer-path`) provides the `connections:` that the project and its layers consume; the lines before it list the connection checks. Earlier failures for the context (pack loading, a `-L` path that does not exist, undefined layer variables) end with the same message.
fix: Read the connection report printed before the message (add `-v` or `-d` for detail). Install the board or device pack that ships a matching layer, point `-L` to a folder with compatible clayer.yml files, or adjust the `connections:` the project consumes; fix any earlier error first.

message: no default rwx memory nor algorithm with ramstart/size was found
title: csolution: no default rwx memory nor algorithm with ramstart/size was found
cause: While writing the run and debug information (cbuild-run.yml), csolution needs a RAM area to run a flash programming algorithm that has no RAM address of its own: a default DFP/BSP algorithm without RAMstart/RAMsize, or a `memory:` entry of the target type with `algorithm:` but without `ram-start:`/`ram-size:`. It falls back to the first default memory with `rwx` access or the first algorithm with RAMstart/RAMsize in the DFP or BSP, and found neither.
fix: For your own algorithm add the RAM to the `memory:` entry under `target-types:` in the csolution.yml, e.g. `ram-start: 0x20000000` and `ram-size: 0x10000`. If the algorithm comes from the DFP or BSP, report the missing RAM information to the pack vendor.

message: no target-set was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no target-set was found with filter '…'
cause: `csolution list target-sets` (or `list targets`) with `-f <words>` found no `<target-type>[@<set>]` entry from `target-types:` - `target-set:` in the csolution.yml that contains all the filter words; `<…>` is the filter. A target type without `target-set:` entries is not listed.
fix: Use part of an existing target-type or set name in the filter, or run without `-f` to see the target sets the csolution.yml defines.

title: csolution: node '…' shall contain sequence elements
cause: A node that must be a list is written as a scalar, a mapping or left empty in a csolution, cproject, clayer, cbuild-pack or cbuild-set YAML file; `<…>` is the node, with file, line and column. The nodes checked are `projects:`, `target-types:`, `build-types:`, `misc:`, `packs:`, `resolved-packs:`, `components:`, `connections:`, `layers:`, `groups:`, `files:`, `setups:`, `linker:`, `executes:` and `input:`. Example: `misc: 1`.
fix: Write the node as a list whose entries start with `- `, e.g. `packs:` followed by `  - pack: ARM::CMSIS`, or remove the empty node.

message: one or more selected contexts are unrelated, redefine the '--context arg [...]' option
title: csolution: one or more selected contexts are unrelated, redefine the '--context arg [...]' option
cause: `csolution run -g <generator>` was called with a context selection that spans contexts the generator cannot serve in one call. A global generator runs for one group of sibling contexts (same generator and generator folder, same device, classified as single-core, multi-core or TrustZone), and a selected context whose project is outside that group is unrelated; the context is named with the message.
fix: Run the generator once per group: narrow `-c`/`--context` to the contexts of one device and generator (e.g. `-c +MultiCore`), or use `-S` with a cbuild-set.yml that holds such a selection.

message: output 'lib' is incompatible with other output types
title: csolution: output 'lib' is incompatible with other output types
cause: The `output:` - `type:` settings that apply to a context combine `lib` with `elf`, `hex` or `bin`; output types from several `output:` nodes (in cproject.yml, setups, clayer.yml) add up. Example: a setup with `type: [elf, hex, bin, map]` and another with `type: lib` that both match the same build type.
fix: Make each context build either a library or an executable: restrict the `output:` nodes with `for-context:`/`not-for-context:` so that `type: lib` never meets `elf`, `hex` or `bin`.

title: csolution: pack path: … does not exist
cause: A `packs:` entry has a `path:` to a local pack folder that does not exist; `<…>` is the resolved path. The path is relative to the YAML file that holds the entry (csolution.yml, cproject.yml or clayer.yml).
fix: Correct `path:` so that it points to the folder that contains the pack's pdsc file, e.g. `- pack: ARM::RteTest_DFP` with `path: ./packs/RteTest_DFP`, or remove `path:` to use the installed pack.

message: pdsc file was not found in: <…>
title: csolution: pdsc file was not found in: …
cause: A `packs:` entry with `path:` points to a folder that exists but does not contain `<Vendor>.<Name>.pdsc` for the pack named in `pack:`; `<…>` is the path. The file name is built from the `pack:` value, so a vendor or name that differs from the pdsc file name also triggers it.
fix: Point `path:` to the folder that holds the pdsc file, and make `pack: <Vendor>::<Name>` match the file `<Vendor>.<Name>.pdsc` there.

message: pname '<…>' does not match any device pname
title: csolution: pname '…' does not match any device pname
cause: A `telnet:` entry under `target-set:` - `debugger:` in the csolution.yml has `pname:` set to a processor name the device does not have; `<…>` is that name. The entry is ignored.
fix: Use one of the device's processor names (shown by `csolution list devices`, after the colon in `Device:Pname`) in `pname:`, or remove the entry.

title: csolution: processing context '…' failed
cause: One or more errors occurred while csolution processed the named context (packs, device or board, components, linker, output types, compiler or other settings). This line only sums them up; the specific errors are printed before it.
fix: Fix the errors reported before this line for the same context, e.g. a missing pack, a component not found or a redefinition, then run again.

title: csolution: processing target-sets list failed
cause: `csolution list target-sets` (or `list targets`) failed because the `-f` filter matched no target set; the line before reports `no target-set was found with filter`.
fix: Loosen or drop `-f` so that it matches a `<target-type>[@<set>]` defined in the csolution.yml.

title: csolution: processor name '…' was not found
cause: The processor part of `device:` (after the colon, as in `device: <Device>:<Pname>` or `device: :<Pname>`) names a processor that the selected device does not have; `<…>` is that name. Single-core devices usually have no processor name at all.
fix: Use a processor name of the device as listed by `csolution list devices` (`Vendor::Device:Pname`), or drop the `:<Pname>` part for a single-core device.

title: csolution: projects not found
cause: The csolution.yml lists no project: `projects:` is missing or empty and there is no `west:` or `cmake:` entry. Only a solution whose target sets contain `images:` without any `project-context:` (an image-only solution) may do without projects.
fix: Add the projects under `projects:` in the csolution.yml, e.g. `projects:` followed by `  - project: ./blinky/blinky.cproject.yml`.

title: csolution: redefinition from '…' into '…'
cause: The compiler selected on the command line with `-t`/`--toolchain` differs from the `compiler:` that the YAML files set for the context; the first `<…>` is the YAML compiler, the second the command-line one. The command line wins, and the context is built with that compiler.
fix: No change is needed if the override is intended. Otherwise drop `-t`, or pass the compiler the YAML sets (e.g. `-t AC6`), or change `compiler:` in the csolution.yml.

message: redefinition from '<…>' into '<…>' is not allowed
title: csolution: redefinition from '…' into '…' is not allowed
cause: A setting that takes a single value is given two different values for the same context at different places (csolution.yml, a target-type or build-type, cproject.yml, a setup or a clayer.yml); the first `<…>` is the value found first, the second the conflicting one. It applies to the parts of `board:` and `device:` (vendor, name, revision or processor), `compiler:` (different names or versions that do not overlap), `optimize:`, `debug:`, `warnings:`, `language-C:`, `language-CPP:`, the `processor:` options, the `linker:` script and regions file, and `output:` - `base-name:`.
fix: Set the value in one place only, or make the values agree; restrict a differing setting with `for-context:` so that only one applies to each context. For the compiler, a version range such as `AC6@>=6.18` combines with `AC6`; `AC6` and `GCC` do not.

title: csolution: regions header file generation failed
cause: csolution tried to generate the memory regions header `regions_<board or device>.h` in the project's RTE device folder, either for a default linker script template or because `linker:` - `regions:` names a file that does not exist, and could not. The header is built from the device memories of the DFP (and BSP); it fails when the target has no resolved device or the file cannot be written.
fix: Make sure the device or board resolves (its DFP is installed and listed under `packs:`) and that the RTE folder is writable. Alternatively provide the regions file yourself and name it in `linker:` - `regions:`.

title: csolution: required packs must be specified
cause: csolution was run with `-l required` (`--load required`), which loads only the packs the project names, but the selected contexts name none: there is no `packs:` entry in the csolution.yml, cproject.yml or clayer.yml and no cbuild-pack.yml with resolved packs.
fix: List the packs under `packs:` in the csolution.yml, e.g. `- pack: ARM::CMSIS` and `- pack: Keil::STM32U5xx_DFP`, or run without `-l required` so that csolution uses the installed packs.

title: csolution: solution created for unknown tool: …
