cause: `created-for:` in the csolution.yml does not have the form `CMSIS-Toolbox@<major>.<minor>.<patch>`; `<…>` is the value. Another tool name, or a version with a pre-release or build suffix such as `CMSIS-Toolbox@2.6.0-rc1`, is not recognised, and the minimum-version check is skipped.
fix: Write `created-for: CMSIS-Toolbox@2.6.0` with the plain three-part version of the toolbox the solution needs, or remove the node.

message: specified device '<…>' is not among board mounted devices
title: csolution: specified device '…' is not among board mounted devices
cause: The context sets both `board:` and `device:`, and the device (`<…>`) is not one of the devices the BSP declares as mounted on that board. csolution builds for the device given, not for the board's device.
fix: If the board carries that device, remove `device:` and let the board determine it, or set `device:` to the mounted device (`csolution list boards` and the BSP show it). Keep the combination only if you deliberately target a different device on the board.

message: target-type '+<…>' does not exist in solution<…>, did you mean '.<…>'?<…>
title: csolution: target-type '+…' does not exist in solution…, did you mean '.…'?…
cause: A `for-context:` or `not-for-context:` entry refers to target type `+<name>`, but the csolution.yml has no target type of that name, so the filter never matches. If a build type of that name exists, csolution suggests `.<name>`: `.` and `+` were mixed up.
fix: Use an existing target type after `+`, or write `.<name>` when a build type is meant, e.g. `for-context: .Debug` instead of `for-context: +Debug`.

title: csolution: target-types not found
cause: The csolution.yml defines no usable target type: `target-types:` is missing or empty, or a `type:` name contains `.` or `+`, in which case an `invalid target type(s)` error lists those names first. The schema check also demands `target-types:`, so the bare message appears mainly with `-n`.
fix: Add at least one target type with a name made of letters, digits, `_` and `-`, e.g. `target-types:` - `type: CM0` with `device: ARMCM0`; rename types that contain `.` or `+`.

title: csolution: unknown access sequence: '…'
cause: A value contains `$<name>$` or `$<name>(<arg>)$` that is neither a defined variable nor a known access sequence; `<…>` is the text between the `$` signs. Known ones include `$Dname$`, `$Pname$`, `$Bname$`, `$Compiler$`, `$Solution$`, `$Project$`, `$BuildType$`, `$TargetType$`, `$TargetSet$`, `$Dpack$`, `$Bpack$`, `$SolutionDir()$`, `$ProjectDir(<context>)$`, `$OutDir(<context>)$`, `$elf()$`, `$bin()$`, `$hex()$`, `$lib()$`, `$map()$`, `$cmse()$` and `$Pack(<pack>)$`, plus variables from `variables:`. Example: `path: $UnknownAccessSequence()$` in a generator file.
fix: Correct the spelling or case of the access sequence, or define the variable under `variables:` of the target type or build type in the csolution.yml.

message: unknown load option: '<…>', it must be 'latest', 'all' or 'required'
title: csolution: unknown load option: '…', it must be 'latest', 'all' or 'required'
cause: The `-l`/`--load` option was given a value other than `latest`, `all` or `required`; `<…>` is that value.
fix: Use one of the three values, e.g. `-l latest`, or leave the option out to use the default pack loading.

message: valid <tracebuffer> elements must be named when more than one is declared
title: csolution: valid <tracebuffer> elements must be named when more than one is declared
cause: The device description in the DFP declares several `<tracebuffer>` elements in its device-wide `<trace>` section and at least one of them has no `name` attribute, so the trace sinks written to the cbuild-run.yml cannot be told apart. It is a flaw of the pack, not of the project.
fix: Nothing to change in the project; the run and debug files are still written. Report the unnamed `<tracebuffer>` to the DFP vendor or update to a DFP version that names them.

title: csolution: variable '…' redefined from '…' to '…'
cause: The same variable is set to different values under `variables:` at more than one level of the csolution.yml, at solution level, in a build type and in a target type; the placeholders are the name, the earlier and the later value. They are applied in that order and the later value wins, so the target-type value takes precedence. A user variable that reuses a built-in name such as `Project` or `BuildType` also triggers it.
fix: Define the variable at one level only, or give it the same value everywhere; rename variables that clash with built-in names.

message: yaml schemas were not found, file cannot be validated
title: csolution: yaml schemas were not found, file cannot be validated
cause: csolution looks for `<type>.schema.json` (e.g. `cproject.schema.json`) next to its executable, in `../etc/` or in `../../etc/`, and did not find the schema for the file named with the message. The file is processed without schema validation. This points to an incomplete CMSIS-Toolbox installation or a csolution binary moved away from its `etc` folder.
fix: Use csolution from a complete CMSIS-Toolbox installation whose `etc` folder contains the *.schema.json files, or reinstall the toolbox. `-n` suppresses the schema check and this warning.

title: packchk M110: Verifying RTE Model failed
cause: Validation of the RTE model built from the PDSC (and any -i reference PDSCs) found invalid items, for example a condition attribute that names an undefined condition. The details follow right after as 'RTE Model reports' messages (M500, M505, M506).
fix: Work through the 'RTE Model reports' lines after M110 and fix each named element (define or correct the condition id, add the missing <processor>, remove duplicates); M110 goes away with them.

title: packchk M204: File not found: '…'!
cause: The specified PDSC file could not be found in the _PATH_ displayed in the message. Correct the path or the filename.
fix: Correct the path or name of the PDSC on the command line; a relative path is resolved against the current working directory.

message: Unable to find PACK.xsd schema file. Searched in '%MSG%' relative to '%PATH%'.   Alternatively use --xsd to specify the location of the schema file.
title: packchk M218: Unable to find PACK.xsd schema file. Searched in '…' relative to '…'. Alternatively use --xsd to …
cause: No --xsd option was given and packchk found no PACK.xsd in ./, ../etc/ or ../../etc/ relative to the folder of its executable (%PATH%), so it cannot run the schema check. The README row for M218 describes the --xsd case, which is M219.
fix: Pass the schema with --xsd <path>/PACK.xsd, or run packchk from a CMSIS-Toolbox installation where etc/PACK.xsd sits next to bin/, or skip the schema check with --disable-validation.

message: Unable to find specified schema file '%PATH%'
title: packchk M219: Unable to find specified schema file '…'
cause: The schema file given with --xsd does not exist (a relative path is resolved against the current working directory). The same message appears when the stored schema path no longer exists when the check starts.
fix: Point --xsd at an existing PACK.xsd, preferably with an absolute path; or omit --xsd so packchk uses the PACK.xsd of its installation (./, ../etc/ or ../../etc/ next to the executable); or use --disable-validation to skip the schema check.

title: packchk M300: … must use '…'
cause: An element text or attribute value in the PDSC contains 'http://', for example <url>, <repository>, the url of a <release>, the name of a <book> or <file>, a board orderForm or an <image> link. %TAG% is the element name for element text, or the attribute name; packchk wants 'https://'.
fix: Change each reported link from http:// to https:// and check that the https address works, e.g. <url>https://www.myvendor.com/pack/</url>.

message: Checking Pack URL of PDSC file failed:   Expected URL : '%URL1%'   Package  URL : '%URL2%'
title: packchk M301: Checking Pack URL of PDSC file failed: Expected URL : '…' Package URL : '…'
cause: The URL specified in the package does not match the value entered for comparison in option `-u`. Check for possible misspellings in both URLs. Refer to [/package/url](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#package_url).
fix: Make <url> start with the URL given to -u (compared without regard to case; trailing slashes of the -u value are ignored), or correct the -u value, e.g. -u https://www.myvendor.com/pack/ with <url>https://www.myvendor.com/pack/</url>.

message: No vendor tag found in the PDSC file. Add the <vendor> tag and provide the vendor name. For example: <vendor>Keil</vendor>.
title: packchk M302: No vendor tag found in the PDSC file. Add the <vendor> tag and provide the vendor name. For …
cause: Vendor name is mandatory required in the package description but was not found in the [/package](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#element_package) element in the PDSC file. Within the parent `<package>` element enter the tag `<vendor>` and add the vendor name. For example: `<vendor>Keil</vendor>`. Refer to [/package/vendor](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#package_vendor).
fix: Add <vendor>MyVendor</vendor> under <package>; the value is also the first part of the PDSC file name (<vendor>.<name>.pdsc).

message: No package name found in the PDSC file. Add the <name> tag and provide the package name. For example: <name>MCU-Name_DFP</name>.
title: packchk M303: No package name found in the PDSC file. Add the <name> tag and provide the package name. For …
cause: Package name is mandatory required in the package description but was not found in the [/package](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#element_package) element in the PDSC file. Within the parent `<package>` element enter the tag `<name>` and add the package name. For example `<name>MCU-Name_DFP</name>`. Refer to [/package/name](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#package_name).
fix: Add <name>MyPack</name> under <package>; it must equal the second part of the PDSC file name (<vendor>.<name>.pdsc).

message: No package URL (<url>-tag and/or value) found in PDSC file!
title: packchk M304: No package URL (<url>-tag and/or value) found in PDSC file!
cause: Package URL is mandatory required in the package description but was not found in the [/package](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#element_package) element in the PDSC file. Within the parent `<package>` element enter the tag `<url>` and add the URL that should be used to download the package. Refer to [/package/url](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#package_url).
fix: Add <url> under <package> with the location the pack is downloaded from, ending in '/', e.g. <url>https://www.myvendor.com/pack/</url>.

message: No releases ("<release>" elements in a <releases>-tag) found in PDSC file!
title: packchk M305: No releases ("<release>" elements in a <releases>-tag) found in PDSC file!
cause: The PDSC has a <releases> element, but it contains no <release>.
fix: Add at least one release, newest first: <releases><release version="1.0.0" date="2026-01-31">Initial release</release></releases>.
doc_cause: At least one package release shall be specified in the PDSC file, but none was not found. Use `<release>` tag to specify release information in `<releases>` element. Refer to [/package/releases/release](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/element_releases.html#element_release).

message: No package description found in the PDSC file. Add the <description> tag and provide a descriptive text. For example: <description>Device Family Pack for  ...</description>.
title: packchk M306: No package description found in the PDSC file. Add the <description> tag and provide a descriptive …
cause: Package description is mandatory required in the package description but was not found in the [/package](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#element_package) element in the PDSC file. Within the parent `<package>` element add the tag `<description>` and briefly describe the package content. Refer to [/package/description](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#package_description).
fix: Add <description>Device Family Pack for ...</description> under <package>; keep it to plain ASCII on one line, within 128 characters, to avoid M387 and M388.

title: packchk M308: Attribute '…' missing on '…'
cause: An element lacks an attribute packchk requires: a <memory> without start or size, a <mountedDevice> without Dvendor or Dname, or a <licenseSet> without id.
fix: Add the attribute named in the message to that element, e.g. <memory name="SRAM" access="rw" start="0x20000000" size="0x00010000"/> or <mountedDevice deviceIndex="0" Dvendor="ARM:82" Dname="ARMCM4"/>.
doc_cause: Element _'TAG2'_ requires attribute _'TAG'_, but it was not found. Add missing attribute.

title: packchk M309: Attribute '…' missing on '…' (when '…' is specified)
cause: Add missing attribute _'TAG'_ or remove the attribute _'TAG3'_ in the element _'TAG2'_.
fix: Give the <memory> both name and access, e.g. name="SRAM" access="rwx", or use the legacy id form instead.

message: Associated File/Path is outside PACK root: '%PATH%'
title: packchk M313: Associated File/Path is outside PACK root: '…'
cause: A file or folder referenced in the PDSC resolves to a location outside the folder that contains the PDSC (the pack root), typically through '../' segments in its path.
fix: Move the file into the pack folder tree and reference it with a path relative to the PDSC that stays inside it, e.g. name="Source/test2.c" instead of name="../ExtFiles/test2.c".

message: Filename '%NAME%' contains whitespaces, this is not recommended
title: packchk M314: Filename '…' contains whitespaces, this is not recommended
cause: A file path referenced in the PDSC (file, book, algorithm, image, svd, example doc, environment load, csolution layer or template) contains a space character.
fix: Rename the file or folder without spaces (use '_' or '-') and update the reference in the PDSC.

title: packchk M316: URL must end with slash '/': '…'
cause: The value of the package <url> element does not end with '/'.
fix: Append the slash: <url>https://www.myvendor.com/pack/</url>.

title: packchk M317: Condition '…': No component found for '…'
cause: An expression inside a <condition> names a component (Cclass, Cgroup, Csub, Cvendor, Cversion ...) that no loaded pack provides. packchk only knows the components of the PDSC under test and of PDSC files passed with -i; %NAME% is the condition id, %NAME2% the expression.
fix: Correct the component attributes in the expression, or pass the PDSC of the pack that provides the component with -i, e.g. packchk MyVendor.MyPack.pdsc -i ARM.CMSIS.pdsc.

title: packchk M318: Attribute '…' must not have '…'
cause: A <compatibleDevice> element of a <board> carries a Dfamily or DsubFamily attribute; packchk wants compatible devices listed one by one with Dname. In the text, %TAG% is the element (compatibleDevice) and %TAG2% the attribute, although it reads 'Attribute ... must not have ...'.
fix: Remove Dfamily and DsubFamily and add one <compatibleDevice> per device, e.g. <compatibleDevice deviceIndex="0" Dvendor="Cypress:19" Dname="S6E1A12C0A"/>.

title: packchk M319: '…': '…' already defined for '…': '…', see Line …
cause: Two <mountedDevice> elements of the same <board> have the same deviceIndex value, which includes two mountedDevice elements that both omit deviceIndex. %NAME2% is the Dname of the earlier one and %LINE% its line.
fix: Give every <mountedDevice> of a board its own deviceIndex, e.g. deviceIndex="0" and deviceIndex="1".

message: File/Path not found: '%PATH%'. Check correct spelling.
title: packchk M323: File/Path not found: '…'. Check correct spelling.
cause: The file or path _'PATH'_ entered in the PDSC file could not be found. Verify the path information.
fix: Correct the path (relative to the PDSC folder, forward slashes, matching letter case) or add the missing file to the pack; %PATH% is the full path packchk looked for.

message: Board referenced in Example '%EXAMPLE%' not found: '[%VENDOR%] %BOARD%'
title: packchk M324: Board referenced in Example '…' not found: '[…] …'
cause: The definition of the board referenced in the example application could not be found. Define the board ([/package/boards/board](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_boards_pg.html#element_board)) or correct the reference information ([/package/examples/example/board](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_examples_pg.html#element_example_board)).
fix: Make the example's <board name="..." vendor="..."/> match a <board> defined in this pack, or pass the BSP pack that defines the board with -i.

message: Path is not conformant: '%PATH%':   Absolute Paths or Drive references are not allowed, use Paths relative to PDSC file.
title: packchk M326: Path is not conformant: '…': Absolute Paths or Drive references are not allowed, use Paths relative …
cause: The path needs to be relative to the PDSC file so that a dependency of a certain file system does not occur.
fix: Write the path relative to the folder of the PDSC, e.g. name="Source/startup.c" instead of "C:/work/pack/Source/startup.c" or "/boards/...".

message: Path is not conformant: '%PATH%':   Backslashes are not recommended, use forward slashes.
title: packchk M327: Path is not conformant: '…': Backslashes are not recommended, use forward slashes.
cause: Paths to files should adhere to the POSIX standard using forward slashes (/).
fix: Replace the backslashes with forward slashes, e.g. Device/Include/device.h.

message: Description not set for Release Information '%VER%'
title: packchk M329: Description not set for Release Information '…'
cause: The release defined through the version _'VER'_ needs a description. Refer to [/package/releases/release](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/element_releases.html#element_release).
fix: Write the release notes as text of the <release>, e.g. <release version="1.2.0" date="2026-01-31">Added USB driver</release>.

title: packchk M332: Condition undefined: '…'
cause: A condition has been used but not defined. Correct the name of the condition or define the missing condition. Refer to [/package/conditions/condition](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_conditions_pg.html#element_condition).
fix: Define <condition id="..."> with exactly the referenced id (spelling and case), or change the condition attribute to an existing id.

title: packchk M334: Config File has no version: '…'
cause: Specified file 'PATH' does not contain version information. It is recommended to specify versions for configuration files. Add attribute version with the file version in the `<file>` tag that defines the _'PATH'_ file in the PDSC. Refer to [/package/.../files/file](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_file).
fix: Add version to the <file attr="config"> element, e.g. <file category="header" attr="config" name="Config/RTE_Device.h" version="1.0.0"/>, and raise it when the file changes.

message: File with category '%CAT%' has wrong extension '%EXT%': '%PATH%'%MSG%
title: packchk M337: File with category '…' has wrong extension '…': '…'…
cause: The extension of the file does not match the file category _'CAT'_ specified in the category attribute. Verify the extension to match the category. Refer to [/package/.../files/file](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_file).
fix: Use the extension that fits the category (header: .h or .hpp; sourceC: .c; sourceCpp: .cpp, .cc or .cxx; sourceAsm: .s or .asm; the package description overview: .md), or change category to match the file.
note: The overview attribute of <description> is not in the 1.7.15 schema copy in the tree (tools/packchk/test/data/schema.xsd).

message: Include Path '%PATH%' must not be a file!
title: packchk M339: Include Path '…' must not be a file!
cause: A <file category="include"> entry does not name an existing folder: it points to a file, or to a path that does not exist.
fix: Set name to the include folder with a trailing '/', e.g. <file category="include" name="Include/"/>; list single header files with category="header" instead.
doc_cause: The path specified contains a filename. Correct the path infomation and remove the filename. Refer to [/package/.../files/file](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_file).

title: packchk M340: Include Path '…' must end with '/'
cause: Include paths must end with a slash or backslash. Verify and correct the path name. Refer to [/package/.../files/file](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_components_pg.html#element_file).
fix: Append '/' to the folder name: <file category="include" name="Include/"/>.

title: packchk M346: Referenced device(s) in '…' not found: '…'
cause: The device or devices specified for the board could not be found. Verify and correct the device name or the board name. Refer to [/package/boards/board/mountedDevice](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_boards_pg.html#element_board_mountedDevice) and [/package/boards/board/compatibleDevice](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_boards_pg.html#element_board_compatibleDevice).
fix: Correct Dname and Dvendor of the <mountedDevice> or <compatibleDevice> to an existing device or variant, or pass the DFP's PDSC with -i so its devices are known.

title: packchk M348: Feature redefined for '…', see Line …: '…'
cause: Within one device-level element (family, subFamily, device or variant), two <feature> elements with the same type, m and name, or two <algorithm> elements with the same identity, apply to the same processor (same Pname, or both to all processors); a <board> can also list the same feature twice.
fix: Remove the duplicate entry, or make the two distinct (different Pname or attribute values) if both are meant.
doc_cause: This feature _'FEATURE'_ has been defined already on the same level in line _'REF\_LINE'_. The feature characteristics defined on line _'LINE'_ overwrite those from _'REF\_LINE'_. Correct the feature ([/package/devices/family/.../feature](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_feature)).

message: Path '%PATH%' does not specify a file!
title: packchk M356: Path '…' does not specify a file!
cause: A <file> element with a category other than "include" names a folder instead of a file, e.g. name="Files/".
fix: Point name at a file; if the folder is meant as include path, use <file category="include" name="Files/"/>.

message: Config File '%NAME%', which gets copied to project, is also found in the include path to the original pack folder. Do not place config header files in the same directory as regular header files. See Line %LINE%
title: packchk M357: Config File '…', which gets copied to project, is also found in the include path to the original …
cause: A configuration file (<file attr="config">) sits in a folder that the pack also uses as include path, either a <file category="include"> folder or the folder of a <file category="header">. A project then sees both its own copy and the original in the pack; %LINE% points to the entry that adds the include path.
fix: Move config files into their own folder (e.g. Config/) that no include or header entry points to and update their name attributes; keep regular headers in the include folder.

message: Family has no Device(s) or Subfamilies: '%FAMILY%
title: packchk M359: Family has no Device(s) or Subfamilies: '…
cause: The device family has no devices or subfamilies. Add the missing information ([/package/devices/family](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_family)).
fix: Add <device> elements (or a <subFamily> with devices) to the <family>, or remove the empty family.

title: packchk M360: Subfamily has no Device(s): '…
cause: A <subFamily> element contains no <device> element.
fix: Add <device> elements to the subFamily, or remove it.
doc_cause: Add the missing information. Refer to [/package/devices/family/subFamily](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_subFamily).

title: packchk M367: Redefined … '…' found, see Line …
cause: Two sibling elements have the same name: for example two <device> elements with the same Dname in one family or subFamily, or two <licenseSet> elements with the same id. %TYPE% says which kind (Family, Subfamily, Device, Variant or id).
fix: Rename or remove the duplicate element.
doc_cause: Remove duplicate device/variant entries. Refer to [/package/devices/family/../device](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_device).

title: packchk M371: … Feature for '…': '…' unknown.
cause: This feature _'FEATURE'_ is unknwon to the specified _'MCU'_. Correct the feature ([/package/devices/family/.../feature](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_feature)) if this is a typo.
fix: Use a feature type packchk knows, spelled exactly, e.g. device features such as "NVIC", "UART", "QFP" or board features such as "ODbg", "LED", "Button": <feature type="UART" n="4"/>. The check runs only when schemaVersion is above 1.1.

title: packchk M376: Schema Version not set!
cause: The <package> element has no schemaVersion attribute.
fix: Add schemaVersion to <package>, e.g. <package schemaVersion="1.7.15" ...>, naming the pack schema version the PDSC is written for.
doc_cause: Set a valid schema version in the PDSC file. Refer to schemaVersion attribute in the [/package](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#element_package).

message: Requirement <%TAG%> '[%VENDOR%] %NAME% %VER%' could not be resolved.%MSG%. Use option -i PackName.pdsc to resolve external dependencies.
title: packchk M382: Requirement <…> '[…] … …' could not be resolved.…. Use option -i PackName.pdsc to resolve external …
cause: The package requires a package with name _'NAME'_ and version _'VER'_ from vendor _'VENDOR'_. That package was not found. Verify the requirement. Use option `-i` to point to the required package. Refer to [/package/requirements/packages](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/element_requirements_pg.html#element_packages).
fix: Pass the required pack's PDSC with -i (e.g. -i /path/to/ARM.CMSIS.pdsc), or correct vendor, name or the version range of the <package> entry in <requirements><packages>.

title: packchk M386: Release date is in future: '…' (today: …)
cause: The date attribute of a <release> is later than today's date on the machine that runs packchk. The README advice 'Set the date to the future' is inverted.
fix: Set date to the actual release date, today or earlier, in YYYY-MM-DD form.
doc_cause: Set the date to the future. Refer to [/package/releases/release](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/element_releases.html#element_release).

message: Description in '%TAG%' is exceeding the recommended 128 (US ASCII) characters.
title: packchk M387: Description in '…' is exceeding the recommended 128 (US ASCII) characters.
cause: The text of a <description> element (of the package, a component, device, example and so on) is longer than 128 characters.
fix: Shorten the description to at most 128 characters and put longer text into the pack documentation; the message is a recommendation and can be suppressed with -x M387.

title: packchk M388: Unsupported character(s) found in '…'
cause: The text of a <description> element contains a character outside printable US-ASCII (0x20 to 0x7E), for example a non-ASCII letter, a symbol such as the euro sign, typographic quotes, or a line break inside the text; %NAME% shows the whole description.
fix: Replace such characters with plain ASCII (e.g. 'EUR', straight quotes) and keep the description on one line.

message: The component '%NAME%' (Line %LINE%) has dependency '%EXPR%' : '%NAME2%' that is resolved by the component itself.
title: packchk M389: The component '…' (Line …) has dependency '…' : '…' that is resolved by the component itself.
cause: A component's condition (directly or through a referenced condition) contains a component dependency that the component itself satisfies, e.g. the component Cclass="C" Cgroup="G" uses a condition with <require Cclass="C" Cgroup="G"/>. %NAME% is the component, %EXPR% the condition and %NAME2% the expression.
fix: Remove the self-matching <require> or <accept> from that condition, or give the component its own condition without it, e.g. split a shared condition into a hardware part and a software part.

title: packchk M392: Redefined Device or Variant '…': …
cause: Multiple defitions of device or variant _'NAME'_ are found. Use unique names for the devices listed in the message _'MSG'_. Refer to [/package/devices/family/../device](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_device) and [/package/devices/family/.../device/variant](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_family_pg.html#element_variant)
fix: Rename one of the device or variant definitions so each name is unique, or remove the duplicate; the message lists every place the name is used.

title: packchk M394: Not Semantic Versioning, ignoring version: '…'
cause: Package version does not follow expected [semantic versioning](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/pdsc_package_pg.html#VersionType). Correct the value specified for the version attribute using correct semantic. Refer to [/package/releases/release](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/element_releases.html#element_release).
fix: Use MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with optional -prerelease and +build parts, e.g. version="1.2.0" or version="1.2.0-rc1".

message: Release %TAG% not consecutive (newest first): '%RELEASEVER%', '%RELEASEDATE%' (prev.: '%LATESTVER%', '%LATESTDATE%', see Line %LINE%)
title: packchk M396: Release … not consecutive (newest first): '…', '…' (prev.: '…', '…', see Line …)
cause: The <release> elements are not ordered newest first by version: a release has a version equal to or higher than the release listed before it. Only versions are compared, not dates; %TAG% is always 'Version'.
fix: Order the releases by strictly decreasing version, newest first, and remove duplicate version entries.
doc_cause: Package releases shall be entered in consecutive way: newest release version and latest date first. Rearrange the releases in the list or correct values for the returned 'TAG' attributes (version or date). Refer to [/package/releases/release](https://open-cmsis-pack.github.io/Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec/main/html/element_releases.html#element_release).

title: packchk M511: Xerxes reports: …
cause: The PDSC does not validate against PACK.xsd: Xerces reports an element or attribute the schema does not allow at that place, a missing required attribute, a value that breaks the schema type or pattern, or XML that is not well-formed. It is also printed as 'Exception: ...' when the schema or PDSC cannot be read. packchk continues with its other checks.
fix: Correct the PDSC at the reported line as the Xerces text says (element spelling and order, allowed attribute values, required attributes). If the element is valid in a newer pack schema, point --xsd at a PACK.xsd of that version.

title: packchk M600: Attribute '…' on '…' is deprecated.
cause: A <file> element uses attr="copy", which packchk reports as deprecated.
fix: Remove attr="copy" from the <file>; if users are meant to get an editable copy in their project, use attr="config" with a version attribute instead.

title: packchk M601: '…' missing on '…'
cause: A required part is missing: <licenseSets> without any <licenseSet>; a <licenseSet> without <license>; a <license> without name or title; in <csolution>, a <clayer> without type, path or file, or a <template> without name, path, file or a <description> child. %TAG% is what is missing, %TAG2% the element that lacks it.
fix: Add what the message names, e.g. <license name="licenses/MIT.txt" title="MIT License"/>, or <clayer type="Board" path="boards/myboard/layers" file="Board.clayer.yml"/>.
note: <csolution>, <clayer> and <template> are not in the 1.7.15 schema copy in the tree (tools/packchk/test/data/schema.xsd); PACK.xsd itself is not in the tree, so these names come from CheckFiles.cpp and the test pack.

title: packchk M602: Attribute '…' already set, see Line …
cause: More than one <licenseSet> in <licenseSets> is marked default; only one license set can be the default. The message is logged without a line number, so its 'see Line' part is not filled in.
fix: Keep default="true" on exactly one <licenseSet> and remove it from the others.

message: Currently no Dcore feature check for '%NAME%'
title: packchk M604: Currently no Dcore feature check for '…'
cause: A <processor> has a Dcore for which packchk keeps no list of required processor attributes (it knows Cortex-M0, M0+, M1, M3, M4, M7, M23, M33, M35P, M52, M55, M85, Star-MC1, SC000, SC300, ARMV8MBL, ARMV8MML and ARMV81MML), for example a Cortex-A or Cortex-R core or a misspelled Dcore. The attribute check (M605) is then skipped for that device.
fix: Nothing to change for a correctly spelled non-listed core; suppress with -x M604 if wanted. If the Dcore is misspelled, use the exact schema value, e.g. Dcore="Cortex-M33".

title: packchk M605: Required Dcore '…' feature '…' not defined
cause: A <processor>, together with what it inherits from family and subFamily, lacks an attribute that packchk requires for its Dcore: Dfpu, Dmpu, Ddsp, Dendian, Dclock and DcoreVersion for every listed core; Dtz additionally for Cortex-M23, M33, M35P, M52, M55, M85, Star-MC1, SC000, SC300 and the ARMV8M/ARMV81M cores; Dmve for M35P, M52, M55, M85, Star-MC1 and ARMV81MML. On devices with more than one processor every processor also needs Pname.
fix: Add the named attribute to the <processor> (or to the family or subFamily level it inherits from), e.g. <processor Dcore="Cortex-M4" DcoreVersion="r0p1" Dfpu="SP_FPU" Dmpu="MPU" Ddsp="DSP" Dendian="Little-endian" Dclock="100000000"/>.

message: Tag '%TAG%' does not allow wildcard specification: '%NAME%'
title: packchk M607: Tag '…' does not allow wildcard specification: '…'
cause: A <mountedDevice> of a <board> uses a wildcard (*, ?, [ or ]) in Dname; a mounted device must name one device.
fix: Replace the pattern with the exact device or variant name, e.g. <mountedDevice deviceIndex="0" Dvendor="ARM:82" Dname="ARMCM4"/>.

title: packchk M608: Memory '…' with '…'='…' must have '…'='…'
cause: A <memory> has startup="1" but its access attribute does not contain 'x' (execute); a startup memory without access is reported too. Memories with id IROM*/IRAM* are exempt.
fix: Add x to the access of the startup memory or move startup="1" to the executable region, e.g. <memory name="Flash" access="rx" start="0x08000000" size="0x00080000" startup="1"/>.

message: Processor '%NAME%': Exact one memory with attribute "startup=1" must be configured, but found %NUM%
title: packchk M609: Processor '…': Exact one memory with attribute "startup=1" must be configured, but found …
cause: Among the memories that apply to a processor of a device (including those inherited from family and subFamily), none or more than one has startup="1".
fix: Mark exactly one executable memory per processor with startup="1" and remove startup or set it to "0" on the others.
note: On multi-core devices the processor name printed in the message accumulates the names of earlier processors (devName is extended inside the loop, ValidateSemantic.cpp:199-208).

message: File category '%CAT%': '%NAME%' redefined in component '%NAME2%', see Line %LINE%
title: packchk M610: File category '…': '…' redefined in component '…', see Line …
cause: The same source, library or object file (category library, object, source, sourceC, sourceCpp, sourceAsm or genSource) is listed in two components with the same file condition, component condition, Cvariant and Cbundle, so selecting both would add the file twice. %NAME% shows packchk's internal key (file name and those values joined by ':').
fix: List the file in one component only; if several components need it, move it into a common component that the others require.

message: Multiple devices or variants defined by '[%VENDOR%] %MCU%'
title: packchk M611: Multiple devices or variants defined by '[…] …'
cause: A <mountedDevice> of a <board> names a device that has <variant> children, so the board does not identify a single device.
fix: Set Dname to the variant that is actually mounted, e.g. Dname="RteTest_ARMCM4_FP" instead of the parent device "RteTest_ARMCM4".

title: svdconv M123: File/Path not found: '…'!
cause: A path given on the command line does not exist: the input SVD file, or the output directory of -o/--outdir when --create-folder is not given. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory.
fix: Correct the path of the .svd file or of the -o directory, or add --create-folder so svdconv creates the output directory.

message: SFR generation is only supported on Windows (requires SfrCC2.exe).
title: svdconv M133: SFR generation is only supported on Windows (requires SfrCC2.exe).
cause: --generate=sfr was used on Linux or macOS. SFR generation runs SfrCC2.exe, which exists only on Windows, so svdconv stops after the intermediate .sfd file and exits with code 2.
fix: Use --generate=sfd on Linux and macOS, or run --generate=sfr on Windows with SfrCC2.exe (from Keil MDK/uVision) in the same directory as svdconv.exe.
doc_cause: Generate SFR output on Windows with SfrCC2.exe installed alongside SVDConv, or use `--generate=sfd` for SFD output.

title: svdconv M202: Parse error: <…> = '…'
cause: svdconv cannot convert the element's value: a number that is not plain decimal, 0x hex or 0b/# binary, a boolean other than true/false/1/0, or a token outside the allowed list (e.g. <usage>, <endian>, <modifiedWriteValues>, <readAction>, <protection>). A leading '+' and the k/M/G/T scale suffix are rejected although the CMSIS-SVD schema pattern allows them.
fix: Write the value in a form svdconv parses: decimal (4096), hex (0x1000) or binary (0b1010) numbers, true or false for flags, and the exact schema token for enumerated values. Replace scaled values such as 4k with 0x1000.
note: Empty values give M205 and <access> values give M233 instead. scaledNonNegativeInteger in CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 is '[+]?(0x|0X|#)?[0-9a-fA-F]+[kmgtKMGT]?'.

title: svdconv M204: Parse Error: '…'
cause: <cpu><revision> is not of the form rNpM with N and M from 0 to 255 (e.g. r0p1). svdconv also reports M325 because no valid revision is set.
fix: Write the core revision as rNpM (N = major, M = minor revision), for example <revision>r1p0</revision>.
note: SvdDimension.cpp:360-363, 393-395 and 425-427 also log M204 for an invalid name/displayName/description expression, but the parser never returns that result at this commit.

title: svdconv M212: Address Block <usage> parse error: '…'
cause: An <addressBlock> <usage> is not one of registers, buffer or reserved. svdconv also reports M202 for that line and leaves the usage unset.
fix: Use <usage>registers</usage>, <usage>buffer</usage> or <usage>reserved</usage> in each <addressBlock>.
note: M212 carries no line number; the M202 that follows does.

title: svdconv M219: C Code generation error: …
cause: The CMSIS header or partition generator (--generate=header, --generate=partition) met a layout it cannot express in C, wrote '#error "MSG"' into the generated file and reports it here; MSG names the problem. Typical texts are 'Unaligned Registers are not supported', 'Cannot generate Register or Cluster ...: Address ... is lower than actual address in struct' (overlapping members), 'Peripheral size ... greater than <dimIncrement>', 'Enumerated Value ... already defined as Value ...' and 'SAU Regions Config / SAU Setup: Number of SAU regions not set'.
fix: Fix the element MSG points to: place a register at an address that is a multiple of its <size>; remove overlaps by correcting <addressOffset>, <size> or the peripheral array's <dimIncrement>; give each <enumeratedValue> a unique <name>; set <sauNumRegions> in <cpu> (1 to 255) before generating the partition file. Look at the validation messages printed earlier (for example M339, M364), which usually name the same cause.
note: Test CheckSauNumRegions_Errors expects two M219 after M364 when generating the partition file.

title: svdconv M224: Deprecated: '…' Use '…' instead
cause: An <access> value uses the deprecated token read or write. svdconv maps it to read-only or write-only.
fix: Write <access>read-only</access> instead of read and <access>write-only</access> instead of write.

title: svdconv M225: Upper/lower case mismatch: '…', should be '…'
cause: A token value has the right letters but the wrong case, e.g. <access>Read-Write</access>, <usage>Registers</usage>, <endian>Little</endian>, <modifiedWriteValues>OneToClear</modifiedWriteValues> or <protection>S</protection>. svdconv accepts the value with a warning, except for <protection> and SAU values, which it also rejects with M202.
fix: Use the exact spelling shown as NAME2, which is the CMSIS-SVD.xsd token, e.g. read-write, registers, little, oneToClear, s/n/p.
note: Error under --strict.

title: svdconv M227: SFD Code generation warning: …
cause: A field wider than 6 bits has <enumeratedValues> with values. The System Viewer (SFD) file builds a drop-down list of values only for fields of up to 6 bits, so the list for this field is left out; MSG names the field and its width.
fix: Nothing in the SVD must change; the field itself is still generated. If the warning should go away, remove the <enumeratedValues> from fields wider than 6 bits, or correct the field's bit range if it is really 6 bits or narrower.

title: svdconv M231: Value <isDefault> not allowed for ….
cause: An <enumeratedValue> inside <dimArrayIndex> uses <isDefault>. Each array index needs its own explicit <value>, so svdconv drops that enumeratedValue.
fix: Replace the <isDefault>true</isDefault> entry with one <enumeratedValue> per array index, each with an explicit <value>.

message: Number of <dimIndex> Elements '%NUM%' is different to number of <dim> instances '%NUM2%'
title: svdconv M308: Number of <dimIndex> Elements '…' is different to number of <dim> instances '…'
cause: An element with <dim> (register, cluster, field or peripheral) has a comma-separated <dimIndex> list whose number of entries differs from <dim>.
fix: Make <dim> equal to the number of <dimIndex> entries, for example <dim>3</dim> with <dimIndex>A,B,C</dimIndex>, and check that <dimIncrement> matches the spacing of the instances.
note: Ranges such as 0-3 or A-D are not counted here: a range whose length differs from <dim> silently yields no index list and no M308.

title: svdconv M314: Address Block: <offset> or <size> not set.
cause: An <addressBlock> lacks <offset> or <size>, and no derivedFrom source supplies it. The block is dropped.
fix: Give every address block all three elements: <offset> relative to the peripheral's <baseAddress>, <size> in bytes and <usage>.

title: svdconv M315: Address Block: <size> is zero.
cause: An <addressBlock> has <size> 0. The block is dropped.
fix: Set <size> to the number of bytes the block spans (for example 0x400), or remove the block.

title: svdconv M325: CPU Revision is not set
cause: The <cpu> section has no <revision>, or its value is not of the form rNpM (for example r0p1, both numbers 0 to 255); a malformed value is also reported as M204.
fix: Add the core revision to <cpu>, for example <revision>r0p1</revision>.

message: Endianess is not set, using default (little)
title: svdconv M326: Endianess is not set, using default (little)
cause: The <cpu> section has no <endian> element; svdconv assumes little-endian.
fix: Add <endian>little</endian> to <cpu> (other allowed values: big, selectable, other).

message: NVIC Prio Bits not set or wrong value, must be 2..8. Using default (4)
title: svdconv M327: NVIC Prio Bits not set or wrong value, must be 2..8. Using default (4)
cause: The <cpu> section has no <nvicPrioBits>, or its value is outside 2..8; svdconv uses 4. The value becomes __NVIC_PRIO_BITS in the generated header.
fix: Add <nvicPrioBits> with the number of NVIC priority bits the device implements, for example <nvicPrioBits>3</nvicPrioBits>.

message: CPU Type is not set, using default (Cortex-M3)
title: svdconv M329: CPU Type is not set, using default (Cortex-M3)
cause: The <cpu> section has no <name>, or a name svdconv does not know (then M202 is reported as well). svdconv falls back to Cortex-M3 and its limits, for example 240 external interrupts.
fix: Set <cpu><name> to a supported core, for example CM0, CM0PLUS, CM3, CM4, CM7, CM23, CM33, CM35P, CM55 or CM85.

title: svdconv M330: Interrupt '…' Number not set.
cause: An <interrupt> has no <value> (its interrupt number). The interrupt is dropped.
fix: Add the interrupt number, counted from 0 for the first device-specific interrupt, for example <interrupt><name>UART0</name><value>5</value></interrupt>.

message: Interrupt '%NAME%' Number '%NUM%' greater or equal '%NAME2%' maximum Interrupts: '%NUM2%'.
title: svdconv M331: Interrupt '…' Number '…' greater or equal '…' maximum Interrupts: '…'.
cause: An <interrupt>'s <value> is equal to or above the number of external interrupts the core in <cpu><name> supports (for example 240 for CM3, 480 for CM33). The message prints that limit minus 1, the highest number allowed. The interrupt is dropped.
fix: Check the <value>: it counts from 0 for the first device interrupt, not from exception number 16. Also check <cpu><name>; if it is missing or unknown, svdconv assumes CM3 with 240 interrupts.
note: Wording: 'Number 240 greater or equal CM3 maximum Interrupts: 239' reads as if 239 were not allowed; 239 is the highest valid number.

title: svdconv M336: … '…' already defined …
cause: Two elements in the same scope have the same name; LEVEL says which: registers or clusters with the same <name> (and <alternateGroup>) in one peripheral or cluster, fields with the same <name> in one register, two <interrupt>s with the same <name> but different <value>s, or the same index twice in a <dimIndex> list. Except for <dimIndex>, the later element is dropped.
fix: Rename or delete one of the two elements (LINE gives the first one). Registers that share a name on purpose need different <alternateGroup>s; an interrupt shared by two peripherals must have the same <value> in both.
note: The 'Enumerated Values Container' variant (SvdField.cpp:440) is not reached: its only caller is commented out (SvdField.cpp:596).

title: svdconv M359: Address Block: <usage> not set.
cause: An <addressBlock> has no <usage>, and no derivedFrom source supplies one. The block is dropped.
fix: Add <usage>registers</usage> (or buffer, or reserved) to the block.

title: svdconv M360: Address Block: found <…> (…) > ….
cause: An <addressBlock>'s <offset> or <size> (TAG) is larger than 0x1000000 (16 MiB). svdconv treats such a number as probably miscalculated but keeps it. Warning by default, error with --strict.
fix: Check the value: <offset> is relative to the peripheral's <baseAddress>, not an absolute address, and <size> is the block length in bytes.

title: svdconv M363: CPU: <sauNumRegions> not set.
cause: <cpu> contains <sauRegionsConfig> but no <sauNumRegions>. The SAU region configuration is dropped.
fix: Add <sauNumRegions> to <cpu> with the number of SAU regions the device implements (1 to 255; 0 together with configured regions gives M387).

message: CPU: <sauNumRegions> value '%NUM%' greater than SAU max num (%NUM2%)
title: svdconv M364: CPU: <sauNumRegions> value '…' greater than SAU max num (…)
cause: <cpu><sauNumRegions> is greater than 255, the most svdconv allows. The value is discarded together with the SAU region configuration, so generating the partition file then also reports M219 ('Number of SAU regions not set').
fix: Set <sauNumRegions> to the number of SAU regions the device really implements (at most 255).

title: svdconv M369: Enumerated Value '…': <value> not set.
cause: An <enumeratedValue> has neither a <value> nor <isDefault>true</isDefault>. The enumerated value is dropped.
fix: Add the value, for example <value>0x1</value> or <value>#01</value>, or mark the catch-all entry with <isDefault>true</isDefault>.

title: svdconv M375: … '…' (<enumeratedValues> '…'): Too many <enumeratedValues> container specified.
cause: A <field> has more than two <enumeratedValues> containers. svdconv allows one container (usage read, write or read-write) or two (one read, one write); the third and later containers are ignored, and M374 follows with the rule.
fix: Merge the extra <enumeratedValues> into the existing ones so the field keeps at most two: one container for all values, or one with <usage>read</usage> and one with <usage>write</usage>.
note: CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 also limits <enumeratedValues> to maxOccurs=2 in fieldType.

title: svdconv M376: … '…' (<enumeratedValues> '…'): '…' container already defined in ….
cause: A <field> has two <enumeratedValues> containers with the same usage. A container without <usage> counts as read-write, so two containers that both omit <usage>, or both say read (or both write), collide; the second one is ignored.
fix: Merge the two containers into one, or set <usage>read</usage> on one and <usage>write</usage> on the other.

title: svdconv M377: … '…' (<enumeratedValues> '…'): '…' container conflicts with '…' ….
cause: A <field> has a read-write <enumeratedValues> container (explicit <usage>read-write</usage> or no <usage>) together with a read or a write container. The read-write container already covers both directions, so the read or write container is ignored.
fix: Keep a single container for all values, or split them into exactly one <usage>read</usage> and one <usage>write</usage> container; add the missing <usage> to the container that has none.

message: XBin Number '%NAME%' too large, skipping evaluation.
title: svdconv M379: XBin Number '…' too large, skipping evaluation.
cause: An <enumeratedValue> <value> uses binary don't-care notation (0b... or #... with x digits) with more than 8 'x' characters. svdconv expands every x into all combinations and refuses more than 8 (256 values), so the value is rejected with M202 and the enumeratedValue is dropped.
fix: Use at most 8 x digits in one <value>: split it into several <enumeratedValue>s, or cover the remaining values with one <enumeratedValue> that has <isDefault>true</isDefault> instead of a <value>.
note: Logged without a line number; the M202 for <value> that follows carries it. Error under --strict.

title: svdconv M381: Interrupt '…' Number '…' greater or equal <deviceNumInterrupts>: '…'.
cause: An <interrupt> <value> is greater than or equal to <cpu><deviceNumInterrupts>. Valid numbers run from 0 to deviceNumInterrupts-1, so the interrupt is dropped.
fix: Correct the interrupt's <value>, or raise <deviceNumInterrupts> to the highest interrupt number plus one.

message: Number of PMU Event Counters set but PMU present not set
title: svdconv M383: Number of PMU Event Counters set but PMU present not set
cause: <cpu> sets <pmuNumEventCnt> but <pmuPresent> is missing or false, so the counter number has nothing to apply to.
fix: Add <pmuPresent>true</pmuPresent> to <cpu> if the core has a PMU, or remove <pmuNumEventCnt>.
note: pmuPresent and pmuNumEventCnt are parsed by svdconv (SvdCpu.cpp:203-215) but are not in the CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 shipped with CMSIS 5.9.0; they belong to a later schema version. The message has no line number.

message: Number of PMU Event Counters (found val: '%NUM%') not set or outside range [2..31]. Ignoring PMU entry.
title: svdconv M384: Number of PMU Event Counters (found val: '…') not set or outside range [2..31]. Ignoring PMU entry.
cause: <cpu> has <pmuPresent>true</pmuPresent> for a core that has a PMU, but <pmuNumEventCnt> is missing or outside the accepted range. svdconv then ignores the PMU entry.
fix: Add <pmuNumEventCnt> with the number of PMU event counters of the core, a value from 2 to 31, e.g. <pmuNumEventCnt>8</pmuNumEventCnt>.
note: The message says [2..31] but the check rejects only <2 or >32, so 32 passes (SvdCpu.cpp:368). pmuPresent and pmuNumEventCnt are parsed by svdconv but are not in the CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 of CMSIS 5.9.0.

title: svdconv M385: PMU not supported for CPU '…'
cause: <cpu> sets <pmuPresent>true</pmuPresent> but the core named in <cpu><name> has no PMU in svdconv's CPU table; only CM52, CM55, CM85, ARMV81MML, SMC2 and SMC3 have one. svdconv drops the PMU setting.
fix: Remove <pmuPresent> and <pmuNumEventCnt> for this core, or correct <cpu><name> if the device really uses a core with a PMU (e.g. CM55 or CM85).
note: No line number in the message. pmuPresent and pmuNumEventCnt are parsed by svdconv but are not in the CMSIS-SVD.xsd 1.3.9 of CMSIS 5.9.0.

message: Name not C compliant: '%NAME%' : Brackets [] found
title: svdconv M386: Name not C compliant: '…' : Brackets [] found
cause: A <name> contains square brackets other than a trailing [%s] on a dim element, e.g. <name>Data[0]</name> on a register without <dim>. Brackets are not valid in a C identifier, so svdconv drops the element.
fix: Remove the brackets (<name>Data0</name>), or describe the element as an array: <name>Data[%s]</name> with <dim> and <dimIncrement>.

message: CPU: <sauNumRegions> set to 0 but regions are configured.
title: svdconv M387: CPU: <sauNumRegions> set to 0 but regions are configured.
cause: <cpu> contains a <sauRegionsConfig> but <sauNumRegions> is 0. svdconv ignores the SAU region configuration.
fix: Set <sauNumRegions> to the number of SAU regions the device implements (at least the number of <region> entries), or remove <sauRegionsConfig> if the device has no SAU.

title: svdconv M389: Specified <deviceNumInterrupts>: '…' greater or equal '…': '…'.
cause: <cpu><deviceNumInterrupts> is larger than the maximum number of external interrupts of the core named in <cpu><name> (svdconv's table: 32 for CM0/CM0PLUS/CM1, 240 for CM3/CM4/CM7/CM23, 480 for CM33/CM55/CM85). svdconv reports it for every <interrupt> and drops each of them.
fix: Set <deviceNumInterrupts> to the real number of device interrupts, which cannot exceed the core's limit, or correct <cpu><name> if the wrong core is named.
note: Message says 'greater or equal' but the check is strictly greater; a value equal to the limit passes (SvdInterruptTest.cpp:112-116). The line number is that of each interrupt, not of <cpu>.

message: CPU: configured number of SAU regions '%NUM%' greater than <sauNumRegions> value: '%NUM2%'
title: svdconv M391: CPU: configured number of SAU regions '…' greater than <sauNumRegions> value: '…'
cause: <cpu><sauRegionsConfig> lists more <region> entries than <sauNumRegions> allows.
fix: Raise <sauNumRegions> to the number of SAU regions the device has, or remove the surplus <region> entries.
